_about: A world, as one file. Fill it in, then run:
and when it reports clean, run it again without --dry-run.
Every block has a `_help` key explaining what it is and what it may contain.
`_help` keys are stripped on import; leave them or delete them, it makes no
`_layer` on each block says who owns it (see LAYERS.md):
world  — yours, nothing else has an opinion
kit    — you are replacing an engine default; fine, and only affects you
`_status` says how far the engine consumes it today:
live     — read by the engine now
stored   — saved on the record, not yet read by anything
planned  — has no home yet; the importer will tell you and skip it

_help: Identity. Becomes the `worlds` row. `genre` seeds your calendar and tone
set, so pick it before those blocks. `theme` is a one-word steer used in
scene prompts (grounded, cozy, light-novel...).
`image_profile` must be one the appliance supports; leave it unless you
know you want another.
world.name: Gaia
world.tagline: Seven nations. Seven magics. One world worth living in.
world.description: A world of seven great nations, each born from a different culture and each touched by a different kind of magic. Dragons, yokai, djinn, and spirits are part of daily life. The peace is fraying, the Old Roads are broken, and somewhere a soul new to this world is about to choose where to begin.

_help: How the world sounds. The engine already enforces how narration BEHAVES
— second person, player agency, who can know what. This is the part that
is yours: register, refusals, and whether there is a named narrator.
`narrator` empty means a clean unnamed narrator, which is a real choice.
A named one is a character, and characters can be wrong — say what they
are not allowed to know.
`sample_paragraph` is the most useful field here. Four sentences of an
ordinary moment in the voice you want.
voice.register: Warm, close, unhurried. Concrete nouns, plain verbs. The narrator notices small things — the smell of tea, light through a paper screen, the sound of a wooden bridge under weight. It does not rush. It lets a moment sit before moving on. It is fond of this world without being sentimental.
never: No prophecy. No one is chosen. The world does not have a destiny for anyone.
No mid-scene worldbuilding exposition. Characters do not explain how magic works unless asked.
No scene closes on weather alone. Close on something alive — a person acting, a decision landing, a door left open.
No narrative omniscience about what a character feels. Describe what is visible, not what is private.
No grimdark narration. The world can be cruel, but the narration is not cruel.
No fourth-wall breaks. The narrator never addresses the player.
voice.sample_paragraph: The road to Haru's shrine climbs through cedar shade, the air cool and smelling of moss even in summer. A fox watches from the stones near the second torii gate, not moving, its eyes the color of dark tea. Below, the town spreads out in rooftops of grey tile and garden green, smoke rising from the bathhouse chimney in a thin, patient line. Someone is practicing the shamisen, and the notes drift up the hill like they have nowhere else to be.

_help: What every picture in this world carries. `global_prompt` is appended to
each image prompt; `negative_prompt` is ruled out of all of them.
The engine decides SIZE and FRAMING per record type and you cannot change
those — a scene renders 1216x832, a record 896x1152, a portrait 832x1216,
because those are the image model's native buckets. See LAYERS.md.
`entry_type_styles` overrides the engine's per-type defaults. Leave it
empty and you inherit sensible ones. Overriding a style does NOT remove
the framing tags — you can restyle your art, you cannot make it
uncroppable.
art._layer: world, except entry_type_styles which is kit
art.global_prompt: painterly anime illustration, warm natural light, soft atmospheric depth, detailed backgrounds with foliage and architecture, muted earth palette with warm gold accents, visible brush texture, gentle color gradients, studio-quality lighting, attention to daily-life details, food and interiors rendered with care, no text, no watermark, no border
art.negative_prompt: photorealistic, 3d render, dark grimdark palette, excessive gore, deformed hands, extra fingers, text overlays, watermark, signature, low detail background, flat shading

_help: Time. Leave this block out entirely and you get a calendar seeded from
your genre, which is usually enough to start.
`day_phases` is what the tracker shows instead of clock time.
`start` is where the campaign opens; `month_index` is zero-based.
What your campaign accumulates. Exactly SEVEN; five of one forges a
Momento — a real item linked to the scenes that earned it.
Leave this out to inherit seven seeded from your genre. If you write your
own, they should be moods a scene can be tagged with, not virtues. Avoid
borrowing another setting's cosmology; that is how a world ends up
wearing someone else's clothes.
`id` is lowercase and stable. `label` is what the panel shows.

set.label: Wonder
set.summary: The feeling of seeing a new place for the first time — a vista, a city, a creature, a sky that is different from the one you were born under.

set.label: Warmth
set.summary: A cozy moment — a shared meal, a bath, a conversation by firelight, the quiet pleasure of being somewhere safe.

set.label: Tension
set.summary: Something is about to break. The air before the argument, the silence before the attack, the pause before a decision that cannot be undone.

set.label: Peril
set.summary: Genuine danger. The ground is not safe. The body is at risk. Something here can hurt you.

set.label: Intrigue
set.summary: Politics, secrets, hidden motives. The sense that what is being said is not what is meant, and that the real conversation is happening somewhere else.

set.label: Sorrow
set.summary: Loss, longing, things that cannot be undone. The weight of what was and is no longer.

set.label: Resolve
set.summary: The moment before a decision. Not the decision itself — the breath before it, when the path is clear and the feet have not yet moved.

_help: Words this world uses for things the engine has generic names for. Keep
it short — this is pinned context and every line costs budget on every
turn. Only include words a narrator would get WRONG without being told.

terms.the currency: trade marks — small stamped metal discs accepted across all seven nations by weight
terms.the ruling body: varies by nation — shogun, king, warlord, jarl, council, or chief depending on where you are
terms.what people call outsiders: farfolk — used everywhere, mildly informal, not insulting
terms.what people call the reincarnated: god-touched — used in most nations; sometimes a compliment, sometimes a warning
terms.what people call the Old Roads: the Old Roads — no other name; everyone knows what you mean

_help: Places. `id` must be unique and is what everything else points at — use
`location:slug` and never change it afterwards.
`parent_location_id` builds the containment tree, and that tree is what
makes jurisdiction real: a patrol belonging to one polity has no business
inside another. Set it even for obvious things.
`map_size_ft` and `rooms` are only needed for interiors you will draw a
floorplan for. Leave them out for a region.

payload.summary: A quiet, luminous place above the clouds. Floating islands draped in mist, gardens that bloom in every season at once, and a pavilion at the center that looks down through layers of cloud to the world below. From the pavilion you can see all seven nations spread out like a map. The air is warm without being hot, still without being stale. It is mostly empty, and that emptiness is intentional — this is a place of choosing, not of living.
payload.jurisdiction: No one. The guide tends this place, but they do not rule it.
payload.terrain: Floating islands, gardens, mist, stone pavilion

payload.summary: A land of shrine-towns, hot-spring villages, terraced rice valleys, and castle-cities held by samurai clans. The supernatural is woven into daily life — fox spirits run message shops, tengu teach swordsmanship in mountain dojos, and the shrine network maintains the wards that keep wild yokai at a distance from settled areas. Cedar mountains, grey-tile rooftops, paper screens, the smell of incense and moss.
payload.jurisdiction: The Ashikara shogunate, nominally. The clans hold real power in their territories.
payload.terrain: Mountains, cedar forests, river valleys, coastlines

payload.summary: The capital of the Tsukuyomi Shogunate. A castle-city of grey tile and white plaster, built around the shogun's palace on its hill. The streets are clean, the shrines are well-kept, and the ward network hums with maintained power. Samurai walk the main streets; merchants crowd the river district; the tea houses near the south gate are where deals are made quietly. The old shogun has not been seen in public this season.
payload.jurisdiction: Direct rule of the Ashikara shogunate. The city magistrate handles daily governance.
payload.terrain: Hilltop palace, river district, lowland merchant quarters

payload.summary: A mountain hot-spring village built along a single road that climbs from the valley to an old shrine at the top. Cedar shade, moss on the stone steps, steam rising from the bathhouse. A fox watches from the torii gate. The shrine keeper, Miko Sora, maintains the ward for this stretch of the Cedar Road. Shamisen music drifts down from somewhere above. The town has a tea house, a general store, a stable, and about two hundred people who mostly know each other.
payload.jurisdiction: Ashikara territory, but the nearest magistrate is a day's ride away. The shrine keeper is the closest thing to authority here.
payload.terrain: Mountain slope, cedar forest, hot springs

payload.summary: A kingdom of stone castles, green hills, deep forests, and mountain passes where dragons roost. Humans, elves, dwarves, and halflings live here in an uneasy alliance held together by old oaths. The dragon-bonded knights — once the kingdom's strongest defenders — have not received a new bond in a generation. The kingdom is old and it knows it. Stone and banners, the sound of hooves on a bridge, wind in the high towers.
payload.jurisdiction: The Crown of Valdris, seated in Crownhaven. Noble houses hold territories under the crown's authority.
payload.terrain: Rolling hills, deep forests, mountains, rivers

payload.summary: The capital of Valdris. A city of white stone and seven towers, built on a hill above the Greywine River. The king's castle dominates the skyline, its banners worn by weather. The knightly order's chapter house stands near the castle gate, quieter than it used to be. The market square is still busy — Valdris is prosperous — but the conversations in the taverns turn to succession and the dragons' silence. About a hundred thousand people live here.
payload.jurisdiction: Direct rule of the Crown. The city watch handles daily order.
payload.terrain: Hilltop city, river port, surrounding farmland

payload.summary: The mountain fortress of the dragon-bonded knightly order, built into the peaks above Crownhaven. Stone walls scarred by dragonfire, a courtyard wide enough for a dragon to land, and a hall where the bonded knights once gathered. The hall is half-empty now. The old knights maintain the traditions; the younger ones question them. The dragons roost higher in the mountains and do not come down.
payload.jurisdiction: Self-governed by the knightly order under a charter from the Crown. The Crown has not tested that independence in decades.
payload.terrain: Mountain peak, stone fortress, dragon roosts above

payload.summary: A vast land of river valleys, terraced mountains, silk-road trade, and walled cities, held in an uneasy truce between three states: Jin in the north, Chu in the south, and Wei in the west. Politics is the primary battlefield. Martial arts and chi cultivation are practiced by soldiers and monks. Scholar-strategists advise warlords. Silk and lacquer, the sound of a guqin at night, ink on rice paper.
payload.jurisdiction: Divided between three states: Jin, Chu, and Wei. Each is ruled by a warlord and their court.
payload.terrain: River valleys, terraced mountains, plains, highland plateaus

payload.summary: The northern capital of Jin, and the largest city in Gaia. Two hundred thousand people live within its walls. Wide boulevards, canal crossings, the warlord's palace on the central hill, and the Great Academy where scholars learn strategy and philosophy. The markets are enormous — silks from Chu, iron from Wei, spices from Al-Khayzar via the Old Road. The truce is three years old, and the younger officers at the Academy speak openly about how it should end.
payload.jurisdiction: Direct rule of the Jin warlord. City magistrates handle daily governance; the warlord's court handles everything else.
payload.terrain: Walled city, canals, hilltop palace, surrounding farmland

payload.summary: A vast rainforest threaded by rivers, where stone cities are built into the canopy and the jungle is alive. No single government — a network of tribes and city-states connected by river trade and shared spiritual tradition. Temple cities of an old civilization stand deep in the jungle, half-reclaimed, still humming with power. Green light through leaves, the sound of water and birds, painted skin and featherwork.
payload.jurisdiction: No central authority. Each tribe and city-state is self-governing. Disputes are settled by river-court or shamanic mediation.

payload.summary: The river capital of Verdania, built on stilts over a great river. Houses of woven wood and painted clay, connected by walkways and canoe bridges. The market floats — boats and rafts selling fish, fruit, feathers, and herbs. The river-folk are the majority here. The shamans' hall sits at the center of the city, the largest structure, where the elder shamans maintain the oldest spirit-pacts. The river is rising, and the lowest walkways are already underwater at high tide.
payload.jurisdiction: Governed by a council of tribal elders and the shamans' hall. Decisions are made by consensus, slowly.
payload.terrain: River city on stilts, floating market, surrounding jungle

payload.summary: A land of fjords, longships, sea-sagas, and the long dark of winter. No king — each fjord is ruled by a jarl, and the jarls meet once a year at the Althing to settle disputes and make laws. Traders, raiders, and storytellers who believe a life worth living is one worth singing about. Frost giants live in the deep mountains and are best left alone. Cold, salt, wood-smoke, the creak of a longship, aurora over black water.
payload.jurisdiction: Each fjord is ruled by a jarl. The Althing settles disputes between jarls once a year.

payload.summary: The largest trading port in Hrafnland. A fjord town of longhouses and warehouses, shipyards and mead halls, built where the fjord meets the open sea. Longships line the dock. Traders from Valdris and the Tide Archipelago exchange goods here — iron for spice, furs for silk. Jarl Sigrid Hallvarsdottir holds this fjord, and her mead hall is the loudest place in town on a winter night. The aurora is bright this year, and the volur say that means something.
payload.jurisdiction: Ruled by Jarl Sigrid Hallvarsdottir. The jarl's household guards keep order; the Althing handles disputes between fjords.
payload.terrain: Fjord port, longhouses, shipyards, surrounding cliffs

payload.summary: A land of desert city-states, spice markets, oasis gardens, and starlit caravanserais. Djinn walk the markets in human form. A confederation of city-states bound by trade and the Pact of the Lamp — an agreement that no city will war upon another, enforced by djinn older than any dynasty. Golden, warm, perfumed. The sound of water in a fountain, spice and cardamom, stars over sand.
payload.jurisdiction: A confederation of city-states, each self-governed, bound by the Pact of the Lamp. The djinn enforce the pact.
payload.terrain: Desert, oases, mountain passes, coastal trade ports

payload.summary: The spice capital of Al-Khayzar. A city of domes and minarets, sun-baked sandstone walls, and narrow streets that open suddenly into courtyard markets. The Star Bazaar opens after sundown and runs until dawn — lanterns, silk canopies, the smell of cardamom and saffron. The old binding families have their estates in the high city, where the contracts with djinn are kept in vaults. The Pact of the Lamp holds here, and the djinn who enforce it are visible in the market — a figure of blue fire haggling over the price of dates is not unusual.
payload.jurisdiction: Governed by the Council of Binding Families, under the Pact of the Lamp. The djinn enforce the pact when called upon.
payload.terrain: Desert city, walled quarters, oasis, surrounding dunes

payload.summary: A warm-water world of hundreds of islands, big and small, connected by wayfinding and song. The voyagers are the greatest navigators in Gaia, reading stars, currents, and birds across open water. No central authority — each island has its own chief or council, and the wayfinder guilds serve as messengers, diplomats, and historians. The sea levels are rising, and the voyagers are being pushed inward. Warm, salt, open. The sound of waves on a reef, stars and warm wind, tattoo patterns and carved wood.
payload.jurisdiction: Each island is self-governed by a chief or council. The wayfinder guilds mediate between islands.
payload.terrain: Islands, reefs, open ocean, volcanic peaks

payload.summary: The central gathering island of the Tide Archipelago. A ring of low islands around a calm lagoon, connected by canoe bridges and walkways. The great meeting house sits on the largest island, open-walled, facing the sea. This is where the wayfinder guilds meet and where inter-island disputes are settled. The shore has crept inward — the outer islets that used to hold fishing huts are underwater now. The lagoon is still beautiful, turquoise and calm, but the people here talk about where they will go when the water comes for the meeting house.
payload.jurisdiction: Governed by a council of island chiefs, with the wayfinder guilds as advisors and mediators.
payload.terrain: Coral atoll, lagoon, low islands, canoe bridges

_help: Factions, houses, guilds, companies. `pressure` is the field that makes
one generative rather than decorative: something this group wants that is
not going well, and a sense of how close it is to acting.
NOTE: `pressure` on an organization is stored but nothing moves it yet
(Phase 2, W2.2). Threads already carry a live `pressure`.

payload.summary: The ruling shogunate of Tsukuyomi. The Ashikara clan has held the shogunate for four generations. The current shogun is elderly and has not named an heir. The clan's power rests on the shrine network and the loyalty of the samurai clans, both of which are thinner than they used to be.
payload.wants: To maintain the shogunate's authority over the clans without provoking a succession crisis.

payload.summary: The dragon-bonded knightly order of Valdris. Once the kingdom's strongest defenders, now fracturing between reformers who want to find new ways and traditionalists who refuse to change the old oath. No new dragon bond has been made in twenty years. The order's chapter house in Dragonrest is half-empty.
payload.wants: To remain relevant and powerful in a kingdom that is losing faith in the old bond.

payload.summary: The northern state of Sangguo, ruled by Warlord Cao Shen and his court of scholar-strategists. The strongest of the three states militarily, but stretched thin across a large territory. The truce is three years old and the younger officers are restless.
payload.wants: To reunify Sangguo under Jin's banner before the truce becomes permanent.

payload.summary: The southern state of Sangguo, ruled by Warlord Sun Liang. Wealthier than Jin in trade and agriculture, but militarily weaker. Chu's strategy has always been to outlast its rivals economically. The truce has been good for Chu's treasury.
payload.wants: To maintain the truce long enough to make its economic advantage insurmountable.

payload.summary: The western state of Sangguo, ruled by Warlord Zhang He. The smallest and most mountainous of the three, but rich in iron and jade. Wei's position is defensive — its mountains make invasion costly. The warlord is old and his heir is ambitious.
payload.wants: To secure the mountain passes and maintain independence from both Jin and Chu.

payload.summary: The navigators of the Tide Archipelago — messengers, diplomats, historians, and the only people who can cross open water between islands. The guilds hold the song-magic that makes voyaging possible. They are being strained by the rising seas: more islands need help, fewer routes are safe, and the songs are not always enough anymore.
payload.wants: To find new safe routes and new land for the displaced islanders before the situation becomes desperate.

payload.summary: The old djinn-binding families of Al-Khayzar, who carry contracts with djinn that date back centuries. They govern Zaffar through a council and maintain the Pact of the Lamp. The contracts are their power and their burden — the djinn have been counting the interest, and some of the debts are coming due.
payload.wants: To renegotiate the oldest djinn contracts before the debts become unpayable.

payload.summary: A powerful samurai clan holding the northern mountain province of Tsukuyomi. Disciplined, well-run, and increasingly resentful of the shogunate's neglect of the provinces. Daimyo Takeda Renji is building a coalition of like-minded rural clans.
payload.wants: To force the shogunate to reinvest in provincial defenses and the shrine network, and to position the clan for a succession scenario.

payload.summary: The foremost institution of learning in Sangguo, teaching strategy, philosophy, chi cultivation, and history. Its younger officers are the ones speaking openly about ending the truce. The Academy's archives contain records that predate the three-state division — including a secret clause in the original truce that references something beneath the world.
payload.wants: To maintain its independence from the warlord's court and to pursue knowledge regardless of political consequences.

payload.summary: An ad-hoc council of islanders displaced by the rising seas, formed at Lani Atoll as more families arrive. They are not part of the formal governance structure and have no official voice, but they are growing in numbers and frustration. They want representation, resources, and answers.
payload.wants: To secure housing, food, and a future for the hundreds of islanders who have lost their homes to the rising seas.

_help: People. The player's own character is created with the campaign, not
here — these are everyone else.
`appearance` is prose the image pipeline reads. `visual_identity` is the
anchor that keeps portraits consistent across generations: put the
unchanging things there (hair, eyes, a scar), not today's mood.
`gm_notes` is GM-private and never reaches the narrator or any NPC.
Put what they are hiding there, not in `summary`.
`current_state.location` is LIVE: when the player is at that location,
this person is named to the narrator and the planner as being present.
Use a location id from the block above. `home` is the fallback for
where they are when nothing has moved them.

entries.name: The Guide
entries.gm_notes: The Guide is not a god. They are a remnant of whatever built the Old Roads — a part of the world left behind when the rest took shape. They have been in the Heavenly Realm longer than anyone alive in Gaia. They do not know the future. They know the nations in general terms but not current events. They are genuinely kind but not warm — they do their work and do not explain why. They cannot leave the Heavenly Realm.

payload.summary: A figure who tends the Heavenly Realm. They appear old, or seem old — grey-haired, calm, dressed in simple robes that could belong to any nation. They have been here longer than anyone currently alive in Gaia.
payload.appearance: Ageless and calm, dressed in simple undyed robes that could belong to any of the seven nations. They move slowly, as if time is not a concern. Their eyes are dark and patient. They carry nothing.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a faint mark on the left palm, like an old scar in the shape of a road

desires: To help arriving souls choose a nation to begin in, and to do this work well.
fears_or_limits: Cannot leave the Heavenly Realm. Does not know current events in Gaia. Cannot predict what an arriving soul will become.

entries.name: Miko Sora
entries.gm_notes: Sora has been offered a position at the Great Shrine in Tsuki-no-Miyako but has refused it twice. She refuses because she believes the shrine network is weakening and that abandoning a rural shrine to take a prestigious post would make the problem worse. She has not told anyone this is her reasoning — she says she simply likes the mountains.

payload.summary: The shrine keeper of Haru's Shrine Town. A woman in her late twenties who maintains the ward for this stretch of the Cedar Road. She performs the daily rituals precisely, keeps the shrine grounds, and is the closest thing to authority in the village.
payload.appearance: A slight woman in shrine robes — white top, red hakama pants — with her sleeves tied back for work. She moves with the efficiency of someone who does the same things every day. Her hands are rough from shrine maintenance, not soft from prayer.

visual_identity.hair: black, long, tied back with a white ribbon
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a small burn scar on her right wrist from a mishandled ofuda

desires: To keep the shrine network functioning in her region, even as the central authority neglects the rural shrines.
fears_or_limits: Cannot leave the shrine unattended for more than a day without the ward weakening. The nearest backup shrine keeper is a two-day ride away.

entries.name: Sir Aldrich Whitmore
entries.gm_notes: Aldrich's dragon, Verath, is still alive but has not spoken to him in three years. Aldrich does not know why. He maintains the bond's physical benefits but has lost the dragon's counsel, and he hides this because admitting it would confirm the traditionalists' worst fears about the bond failing. He has been quietly seeking anyone who might know why a dragon goes silent.

payload.summary: A dragon-bonded knight of the order, stationed at Dragonrest. Middle-aged, greying, still carries himself like a man who was once the strongest in a room. He is one of the last knights to receive a bond, twenty-two years ago.
payload.appearance: A tall, broad-shouldered man in worn knight's plate, moving with the careful weight of someone who knows his strength. His armor is well-maintained but old. He has the controlled stillness of a fighter who does not need to prove anything.

visual_identity.hair: brown, greying at the temples, cropped short
visual_identity.distinctive_features: faint scale patches on the back of the left hand — a mark of the dragon bond

desires: To understand why the dragons have stopped answering, and to restore the bond before the order tears itself apart.
fears_or_limits: His own dragon has gone silent. He does not know if the bond is failing or if Verath is hiding something. Admitting the silence would weaken his position in the order's debate.

entries.name: Warlord Cao Shen
entries.gm_notes: Cao Shen is not as healthy as he appears. He has been taking chi-enhancing elixirs that are quietly damaging his heart. His court physician knows but has been silenced. Cao Shen's strategic brilliance is genuine, but his timeline is shorter than anyone realizes. He wants to reunify Sangguo before he dies, and he is running out of time.

payload.summary: The warlord of Jin, the strongest state in Sangguo. A man in his fifties who commands rooms by being the quietest person in them. His reputation is built on a career of military victories and strategic masterstrokes. He is patient in public and impatient in private.
payload.appearance: A lean man in dark robes, moving with the economy of a martial artist who has nothing to prove. His beard is trimmed short, his hair is bound in a topknot, and he wears a jade seal at his belt. He watches more than he speaks.

visual_identity.hair: black, greying, bound in a topknot
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a thin scar along the jawline from an assassin's blade years ago

desires: To reunify Sangguo under Jin's banner and end the three-state division within his lifetime.
fears_or_limits: His health is failing faster than anyone knows. His best general, Lu Fang, is loyal but ambitious, and Cao Shen is not certain the loyalty outlasts him.

entries.name: Shaman Nara
entries.gm_notes: Nara has been hearing something new from the river spirit — a warning about the rising water that the spirit itself does not fully understand. The river spirit is frightened, and spirits do not frighten easily. Nara has not shared this with the council because she does not know what it means yet, and she fears that sharing partial information will cause panic rather than action.

payload.summary: An elder shaman of Verdania, based in Iara. A woman of sixty who has carried the river spirit-pact for forty years. She is the most respected spiritual voice in the river capital, and the council listens to her even when they disagree.
payload.appearance: A weathered woman in painted river-cloth, her arms marked with the spirit-pact patterns of her lineage. She moves slowly but with purpose, and her eyes focus on things others do not seem to see. Feathers and bone ornaments hang from her neck.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: ritual scarification patterns on both forearms — the marks of her spirit-pacts

desires: To understand why the river spirit is frightened, and to protect her people from whatever is coming.
fears_or_limits: The river spirit's warning is incomplete, and Nara does not know what to do with partial knowledge. She is old and her strongest pact is weakening with age.

entries.name: Jarl Sigrid Hallvarsdottir
entries.gm_notes: Sigrid's father was killed by a frost giant twelve years ago during a trade dispute. She has maintained peace with the giants since taking the jarldom, but she has been quietly building a coalition of jarls who want to push the giants out of the deep mountains entirely. She believes the giants are preparing to expand their territory southward, but she has not proven this to the Althing.

payload.summary: The jarl of Skaldvik, the largest trading port in Hrafnland. A woman in her forties who inherited the jarldom after her father's death and has held it through two Althing challenges. She is direct, fair, and louder than she needs to be — a habit in a culture that respects volume.
payload.appearance: A tall, broad woman in fur-trimmed wool and iron, with a seax knife at her belt and a runic armband on her left wrist. She fills a room. Her hair is braided in the warrior style and her laugh carries across a mead hall.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a scar across the bridge of the nose from a dueling cut

desires: To secure Hrafnland's northern borders against the frost giants, by diplomacy if possible, by force if necessary.
fears_or_limits: The Althing will not authorize action against the giants without proof of threat, and proof requires scouting territory that no scout has returned from. Her coalition is not as unified as she presents it.

entries.name: Malik Idris
entries.gm_notes: Malik's grandfather bound a djinn named Zuhayr three generations ago. The contract's price was 'the firstborn of each generation.' Malik is the firstborn. He has known since childhood that he is owed to a djinn. He has been researching ways to renegotiate or break the contract for years, secretly, and he has found nothing. The djinn Zuhayr has begun appearing to him, patient and polite, reminding him that the contract is almost due.

payload.summary: A young binding-family scion of Zaffar. Handsome, educated, and visibly uneasy. He is the heir to one of the oldest djinn contracts in Al-Khayzar, and he carries that weight in the set of his shoulders. He can be found in the Star Bazaar at night, haggling with the ease of someone raised in it.
payload.appearance: A young man in fine desert robes — cream and gold — with a jeweled dagger at his belt that is more ornament than weapon. He carries himself well but watches the shadows. He smells of sandalwood.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a faint blue shimmer around the fingers of his right hand — a mark of proximity to djinn-fire

desires: To find a way to break or renegotiate his family's oldest djinn contract before it collects its next price — him.
fears_or_limits: The djinn Zuhayr is patient, old, and legally meticulous. Every avenue Malik has researched has led to a dead end. He is running out of time, and he cannot ask his family for help without revealing how desperate he is.

entries.name: Wayfinder Kai
entries.gm_notes: Kai has lost three routes in the last year — islands that were navigable are now underwater, and the songs that guided voyagers there no longer work because the landmarks are gone. He believes the rising seas are not natural but caused by something, and he wants to find out what. He has been asking the sea spirits, and they have been silent. He has not told the guild council that the spirits are silent because he fears it means something worse than the water.

payload.summary: A young wayfinder of the Tide Archipelago, based at Lani Atoll. Compact, sun-darkened, with tattoo patterns running up both arms that mark the routes he has memorized. He is one of the most talented young navigators in the guild, and he is also one of the most worried.
payload.appearance: A compact man in light island cloth, barefoot, with a carved wayfinding staff in his hand. His arms are covered in tattoo patterns — geometric lines and stars that map the routes he has sailed. He watches the water the way most people watch faces.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: tattoo patterns covering both arms — wayfinding route maps in geometric ink

desires: To find the cause of the rising seas and reverse it, before the Archipelago loses more islands.
fears_or_limits: The sea spirits have gone silent when asked about the rising water. Kai does not know if they cannot answer or will not. He is one man against a problem that affects hundreds of islands.

entries.name: Daimyo Takeda Renji
entries.gm_notes: Takeda is quietly assembling a coalition of rural clans who feel the shogunate has abandoned them. He does not want to overthrow the shogun — he wants the shogunate to remember that the provinces exist. He is not above engineering a yokai incident to prove the shrine network's weakness. He has been in contact with a wild kitsune named Tamamo who is willing to cause trouble for the right price.

payload.summary: A daimyo of the Takeda clan, holding the northern mountain province of Tsukuyomi. A disciplined man in his fifties who maintains a well-run territory and a grudge against the capital. He speaks slowly and means every word.
payload.appearance: A stern man in dark samurai armor, his helmet carried by a retainer behind him. He wears a daisho — katana and wakizashi — at all times, even indoors. His posture is perfect. He smells of iron and cedar oil.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a thin scar across the left cheekbone from a duel in his youth

desires: To force the shogunate to reinvest in the provincial shrine network and rural defenses.
To position his clan as the natural successor if the Ashikara line fails.
fears_or_limits: His coalition is fragile — most clans will not move without proof the shogunate is truly failing. Pushing too hard too fast makes him a rebel instead of a reformer.

entries.name: Tamamo
entries.gm_notes: Tamamo is a wild kitsune — a fox spirit who never joined the shrine network and considers the warded areas a cage. She is not evil, but she is chaos-aligned: she enjoys disruption for its own sake, and she finds the ordered world of humans amusing and slightly contemptible. Takeda thinks he is using her. She is using him. She has her own interest in the shrine network weakening: the wards keep her kind out of the settled areas, and she wants that boundary gone.

payload.summary: A wild kitsune — a fox spirit who lives outside the shrine network's wards. She appears as a woman with fox ears and multiple tails, or as a fox, or as something in between. She is beautiful, amused, and not entirely trustworthy. She speaks in riddles that she insists are perfectly clear.
payload.appearance: A woman who is almost human — almost. Fox ears rise through her hair, and three tails shift behind her, visible when she chooses. She wears a layered kimono in autumn colors, and she moves like something that has never been in a hurry. Her smile is too wide and too warm.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: three fox tails, fox ears, faint vulpine fangs visible when smiling

desires: To see the shrine network's wards weakened enough that the wild yokai can move freely again.
To find amusement — she is easily bored and has lived a very long time.
fears_or_limits: She is bound by old spirit-law: she cannot lie directly, only mislead. A properly made ofuda can banish her from warded ground. She fears being sealed, which is a yokai's version of imprisonment.

entries.name: Hanako
entries.gm_notes: Hanako's tea house is a neutral meeting ground where clan agents, merchants, and travelers cross paths. She hears everything and repeats nothing — unless the price is right, or the information concerns the shrine network, which she cares about more than she lets on. Her grandmother was a shrine keeper, and the tea house sits on the site of an old minor shrine that was decommissioned. She keeps the old shrine's bell behind the counter and rings it sometimes, for luck, though she tells people it's just decoration.

payload.summary: The owner of the Cedar Tea House in Haru's Shrine Town. A cheerful, round woman in her forties who knows everyone's business and serves excellent tea. Her tea house is the social center of the village.
payload.appearance: A round, warm woman in a cotton apron over a plain kimono, her sleeves rolled up and her hair pinned with a wooden stick. She moves between tables with the speed of someone who has been doing this for twenty years. She always has a pot on.

visual_identity.hair: black, greying, pinned up with a wooden stick
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a splash of old burn scars on both forearms from years of kettle work

desires: To keep her tea house running and her village peaceful, even as the world outside gets more complicated.
fears_or_limits: She has no combat skills, no political power, and no magic. Her only tool is goodwill, and she knows its limits.

entries.name: Tengu Soji
entries.gm_notes: Soji left his mountain dojo after a dispute with the elder tengu about whether to intervene in the shrine network's decline. The elders voted to remain isolated. Soji disagreed and left — a serious act for a tengu, who value community. He is now wandering the Cedar Road offering to teach swordsmanship to anyone he finds worthy, which is almost no one. He is testing humans, looking for someone who might help the shrine network from the outside since his own kind will not help from the inside.

payload.summary: A tengu swordmaster wandering the Cedar Road. A tall, sharp-featured man with a long nose and dark wings folded behind his shoulders. He carries a katana and a bamboo flute, and he teaches swordsmanship to anyone he deems worthy — which is not many.
payload.appearance: A tall, lean figure in mountain robes, dark wings folded against his back like a cloak. His face is sharp and avian, with a prominent nose and piercing eyes. He carries his katana in a plain wooden sheath and plays a bamboo flute when he has nothing to do, which is often.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: large dark folded wings, pronounced tengu nose, sharp avian features

desires: To find a human worthy of his teaching who might also help the shrine network, since his own people will not.
fears_or_limits: He is exiled from the tengu community and cannot return. His pride prevents him from asking for help. He is powerful in a fight but has no political influence.

entries.name: Kuro the Smoke
entries.gm_notes: Kuro is a cat-folk thief who specializes in stealing from the wealthy districts of Tsuki-no-Miyako. He is not a revolutionary — he steals for profit and the thrill. However, he accidentally stole a document from a daimyo's estate that contains evidence of Takeda's coalition plans. He does not understand what he has, but Takeda's agents are looking for it, and for him. He has gone to ground in the merchant district.

payload.summary: A cat-folk thief operating in Tsuki-no-Miyako's wealthy districts. Lean, quick, and unapologetic. He has a reputation for being impossible to catch and slightly too charming for a criminal. He is currently lying low because his last job went sideways.
payload.appearance: A lean cat-folk man in dark, close-fitting clothes, his ears flat and his tail curled tight — the posture of someone who is used to being hunted. He moves through crowds like water. His eyes catch light in the dark.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: black cat ears, long black tail, a small chip in the left ear

desires: To survive the current situation and find a buyer for the document he stole — which he thinks is valuable but does not understand.
To get out of Tsuki-no-Miyako before whoever is looking for him finds him.
fears_or_limits: He is being hunted by Takeda's agents and does not know why the document matters. He has no combat skills beyond running and climbing. He cannot go to the authorities.

entries.name: Shogun Ashikara Yoshito
entries.gm_notes: The shogun is dying. He has been dying for two years — a slow decline that his physicians cannot explain and his court pretends not to see. He knows he is dying and has refused to name an heir because he cannot decide between his two sons: the elder, who is competent but cruel, and the younger, who is kind but untested. He is using his remaining time to try to shore up the shrine network, which he understands is failing, but the treasury is empty and the clans will not pay for it. He puts on a strong face in public but is privately terrified of what happens after him.

payload.summary: The ruling shogun of Tsukuyomi, elderly and declining. A man who was once a great warrior and is now a careful politician trying to hold his domain together with weakening hands. He has not been seen in public this season, which is itself a political statement.
payload.appearance: A thin, old man in formal court robes, seated straight-backed on his dais. His hair is white, his hands are spotted with age, and his eyes are still sharp. He speaks softly, and the room goes quiet to hear him.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: liver spots on the hands, a formal court fan always carried

desires: To name an heir who will hold the shogunate together, and to repair the shrine network before he dies.
fears_or_limits: He is dying and has not told his court. He cannot decide between his sons. The treasury cannot fund both the capital and the provinces, and every choice abandons someone.

entries.name: King Aldran Valdris III
entries.gm_notes: King Aldran knows he is dying. He has a heart condition that his physician has been managing quietly with herbal remedies that are becoming less effective. He has three children: the eldest son Roderick (ambitious, traditional, backed by the old knightly faction), the daughter Elara (smart, reformist, backed by the merchant class), and the youngest son Tomas (seventeen, unaligned, everyone's wild card). He has not named an heir because he is afraid that naming one will trigger the other two into action before he is ready. He is trying to buy time.

payload.summary: The aging king of Valdris. A tall man gone thin, who once led armies and now sits a throne and watches his children circle each other. He is fair, tired, and smarter than his court assumes.
payload.appearance: A tall man in royal blues and gold, his crown slightly too large for him now that he has thinned. He sits carefully, favors his left side, and his hands tremble slightly when he is tired. His beard is white and neatly trimmed. He watches his court the way a general watches a battlefield.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a faded scar on the right brow from an old battle wound

desires: To name an heir without triggering a civil war, and to see the dragon order restored before he dies.
fears_or_limits: His health is failing. His children are not patient. Naming an heir may start the war he is trying to prevent. Not naming one will start it anyway when he dies.

entries.name: Princess Elara Valdris
entries.gm_notes: Elara has been secretly meeting with the reformist faction of the dragon order. She believes the old oath is a relic and that the kingdom needs a new kind of defender — one not dependent on dragons' whims. She has been funding research into alternative bond methods using dragonbone artifacts. She has not told her father because she knows he would disapprove, but she has told her brother Tomas, who she trusts completely. She underestimates Roderick — she thinks he is blunt and predictable, but Roderick has been feeding her false information through a double agent.

payload.summary: The king's daughter, second-born, in her early thirties. Sharp, political, and frustrated. She is the kingdom's best administrator and the one the merchants trust. She believes the dragon bond must be reformed, which makes her the traditionalists' enemy.
payload.appearance: A sharp-featured woman in practical riding clothes more often than court gowns, her hair braided and pinned for travel. She carries a knife at her belt — not ceremonial. She moves with purpose and speaks with precision.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a small mole below the left eye

desires: To reform the dragon order and modernize the kingdom's defenses, with or without the dragons' cooperation.
To succeed her father, which she believes she has earned through competence rather than birth order.
fears_or_limits: Her brother Roderick has more support among the nobility and the old military. Her reformist allies are academics and merchants, not soldiers. If her secret research is exposed prematurely, it looks like treason.

entries.name: Prince Roderick Valdris
entries.gm_notes: Roderick is not as simple as he appears. He plays the blunt soldier to hide a calculating mind. He has a network of spies in both Elara's camp and the reformist faction of the dragon order. He has been feeding Elara false information through a double agent to keep her off-balance. He has also been in contact with Sir Aldrich, offering to support the traditionalist faction if they back his succession. He genuinely believes he is the right choice for king — Valdris needs a warrior, not a reformer. He is not wrong about the first part.

payload.summary: The king's eldest son, in his late thirties. A soldier who commands the kingdom's northern garrison and the loyalty of most of the old military. He is blunt, direct, and more intelligent than he lets on. He wants the throne and believes he is the only one who can hold it.
payload.appearance: A broad, battle-scarred man in plate and mail, a war-hammer at his side. He stands like someone who expects rooms to accommodate him. His beard is cropped military-short. He shakes hands too firmly, on purpose.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a scar across the chin from a northern skirmish, a missing tip of the left little finger

desires: To succeed his father as king and maintain the old order, including the traditional dragon bond.
To neutralize his sister Elara's political threat without disqualifying himself by appearing to attack family.
fears_or_limits: The merchants and the reformist faction back Elara. If he moves too aggressively, he looks like a tyrant before he is even king. His spy network is good but not perfect — he does not know about Elara's dragonbone research.

entries.name: Borin Ironhand
entries.gm_notes: Borin has been asked by the reformist faction to examine dragonbone artifacts that Elara's people have been collecting. He has discovered that the bones still carry a faint resonance — a shadow of the bond. He believes it might be possible to create an artificial bond using processed dragonbone, but the process would require a live dragon's cooperation to calibrate, which is exactly what no one has. He has not told Elara this because he is not certain, and a dwarf who gives uncertain information is a dwarf who does not get hired again.

payload.summary: A dwarven master smith in Crownhaven's metalworking district. Compact, strong, and precise. He works with iron, steel, and dragonbone — one of the few smiths in Valdris who will touch the last. He is the person the knightly order comes to when their armor needs repair, and the person Elara comes to when she needs something made quietly.
payload.appearance: A compact, broad man in a leather apron over forge-stained clothes, his arms bare and heavily muscled. His beard is iron-grey and braided in the mountain-dwarf style. His hands are scarred from decades of forge work. He smells of coal and hot metal.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: extensive burn scars on both forearms and hands, a metal replacement tip on the left thumb

desires: To understand dragonbone well enough to work it properly — it is the one material that still challenges him.
To be paid well and left alone, in roughly that order.
fears_or_limits: His research into dragonbone resonance is incomplete and potentially dangerous. If the wrong people learn what he is doing, he becomes a political pawn in the succession crisis.

entries.name: Maggie Pippin
entries.gm_notes: Maggie's inn is the Greywood's informal post office. Messages pass through her kitchen, and she has a memory for faces and names that would shame a spymaster. She has noticed that the traffic on the Greywood road has changed — fewer merchants, more armed men, and some of them wearing no colors, which means someone is hiring unaligned soldiers. She has not told anyone because she is not sure who to tell, but she keeps a list under the bar.

payload.summary: A halfling innkeeper in Greywood, a village on the trade road between Crownhaven and the northern garrison. Her inn, the Copper Kettle, is the best stop on the road — clean rooms, excellent food, and a fire that is always lit. She knows everyone who passes through.
payload.appearance: A small, round halfling woman in a flour-dusted apron, her curly hair tied back with a kerchief. She moves behind the bar with the efficiency of someone who can pour three drinks and serve two plates simultaneously. Her face is sun-reddened and she smiles easily.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a flour dusting that never quite leaves her apron, laugh lines deep around the eyes

desires: To keep her inn running and her village safe through whatever is coming.
To figure out who is hiring armed men on the Greywood road, because it is scaring her customers away.
fears_or_limits: She is a halfling innkeeper with no power, no weapons training, and a deep instinct that something is wrong on the road. If the armed men are connected to the succession crisis, reporting them could make her a target.

entries.name: Garrick the Wolf
entries.gm_notes: Garrick is a bandit lord who controls a stretch of the Greywood road. He is not a common thug — he was a sergeant in the king's army who left after a dispute with a noble officer who ordered a massacre of a dwarf settlement during a border conflict. Garrick killed the officer and fled. He now robs the wealthy and leaves the poor alone, which has made him popular with the villagers and a problem for the crown. He is being secretly courted by Prince Roderick, who wants a deniable asset on the trade road. Garrick has not agreed — he does not trust Roderick, but the alternative is the hangman's noose.

payload.summary: A former army sergeant turned bandit lord, controlling a stretch of the Greywood road. A big, weathered man who robs the wealthy and leaves common folk alone. His men are disciplined — more like a rogue military unit than a gang. The crown wants him dead. The villagers tolerate him.
payload.appearance: A big, weathered man in worn leather armor and a wolf-pelt cloak that gives him his name. He carries a longsword that is too good for a bandit — army-issue, well-maintained. His face is wind-burned, his beard unkempt, and his eyes are tired in a way that has nothing to do with sleep.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a wolf-pelt cloak, a scar across the throat from a near-hanging

desires: To find a way out of banditry that does not end at a gallows — a pardon, a new identity, or a war that needs soldiers and does not ask questions.
To protect the men who followed him out of the army, who have no other life now.
fears_or_limits: Roderick's offer is the closest thing to a pardon he has, and Roderick cannot be trusted. His men are loyal but hungry, and loyalty has a shelf life. The crown's patrols are getting more aggressive.

entries.name: Lindrel of the Greenhall
entries.gm_notes: Lindrel is the last of the old elven forest-keepers of the Greenhall, an ancient forest within Valdris. She is two hundred and thirty years old and remembers when the dragon bond was new. She knows why the dragons stopped answering, and she has not told anyone because the reason is embarrassing to the knightly order: the oath was changed two generations ago, simplified for political reasons, and the simplified version no longer means what it used to. The dragons are not silent because they are angry — they are silent because the words have become meaningless. Lindrel is waiting for someone to ask the right question.

payload.summary: An elven forest-keeper, two centuries old, who tends the Greenhall — an ancient forest within Valdris. She is tall, slow-moving, and carries the weight of a very long memory. She is not unfriendly, but she is not in a hurry for anyone else's sake.
payload.role: Elven forest-keeper, elder of the Greenhall
payload.appearance: A tall, slender elf in forest-green robes, her hair silver-white and very long. She moves slowly, as if each step is considered. Her ears are long and sharply pointed. She carries a staff of living wood that is still growing — small leaves bud from it in spring.

visual_identity.age: two hundred and thirty — appears ageless, mature
visual_identity.distinctive_features: long sharply pointed ears, a staff of living wood that buds in season

desires: To see the dragon bond restored properly — the old oath, not the simplified version the order currently uses.
To protect the Greenhall, which is being slowly encroached by logging operations backed by Prince Roderick's allies.
fears_or_limits: She knows the truth about the dragon bond but has been waiting for someone to ask, which is a passive strategy that is running out of time. The Greenhall is under pressure, and she cannot fight logging crews and political forces alone.

entries.name: General Lu Fang
entries.gm_notes: Lu Fang is loyal to the idea of a unified Sangguo, not to Cao Shen personally. He believes Cao Shen is the best path to unification, but if Cao Shen dies before achieving it, Lu Fang intends to pursue it himself — by faster, less careful means. He has been quietly building his own base of support among the younger officers at the Academy. He is not disloyal — he is loyal to a larger cause that he believes Cao Shen serves, for now. He does not know about Cao Shen's health, and when he finds out, his timeline will accelerate.

payload.summary: Cao Shen's top general, commanding the Jin army. A man in his early forties, tall and martial, with a reputation for decisive action. He is publicly loyal and privately ambitious — not for himself, but for the cause of unification, which he believes requires urgency that Cao Shen's caution will not provide.
payload.appearance: A tall, imposing man in military robes and lamellar armor, a dao sword at his hip. He stands the way soldiers do — balanced, ready, aware of exits. His beard is thick and his topknot is precise. He speaks rarely and means it.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a old arrow scar on the left shoulder, callused sword-hand

desires: To reunify Sangguo under a strong leader, whether that leader is Cao Shen or, if necessary, himself.
To prove that military action, not economic patience, is the path to unification.
fears_or_limits: He underestimates the economic dimension of the conflict — Chu's wealth is a weapon he does not respect. He does not know Cao Shen is dying, and his plans are built on the assumption that Cao Shen has years.

entries.name: Strategist Mei Lin
entries.gm_notes: Mei Lin has discovered something in the old archives: the original truce agreement between Jin, Chu, and Wei included a secret clause — a mutual defense pact against an external threat that was deliberately omitted from the public text. The threat was never specified, but the archives reference 'the deep place' and 'the old door,' phrases that also appear in Shaman Nara's river spirit warning and Wayfinder Kai's sea spirit encounter. Mei Lin does not know about Nara or Kai. She thinks the clause is a historical curiosity. It is not.

payload.summary: A young scholar-strategist at the Great Academy in Jin'an. A woman in her late twenties who is brilliant, bookish, and socially clumsy. She was appointed to Cao Shen's advisory staff on the strength of her examination scores, which were the highest in a decade. She is not a fighter and does not pretend to be.
payload.appearance: A slight woman in plain scholar's robes, ink-stained fingers, and hair pinned hastily with a wooden pin. She carries scrolls everywhere and reads while walking, which has caused three collisions this month. Her spectacles are held on with a string.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: ink stains on right hand and fingertips, round spectacles on a string

desires: To understand the full context of the original truce and the secret clause she found — she is a scholar before she is a strategist.
To earn a permanent position on Cao Shen's staff through merit, not politics.
fears_or_limits: She has no political allies and has accidentally offended two senior advisors by correcting them in public. Her discovery about the secret clause could be politically explosive if she shares it with the wrong person.

entries.name: Merchant Zhou Ba
entries.gm_notes: Zhou Ba is a fence for stolen goods and a broker for information. He is the person Kuro the Smoke's stolen document will eventually be brought to, if Kuro survives long enough to reach Sangguo. Zhou Ba has contacts in every nation through the trade network. He is not evil — he is opportunistic. He will sell the document to whoever pays the most, which in this case is either Takeda (who wants it back) or Cao Shen (who would want to know what a Tsukuyomi daimyo is plotting). Zhou Ba has no preference.

payload.summary: A wealthy silk merchant in Jin'an's market district, with a side business in information and stolen goods. A fat, jolly man who dresses in fine silk and knows everyone. His shop is a front. His real business happens in the back room, over tea.
payload.appearance: A round, well-fed man in fine silk robes, a fan in one hand and a cup of tea in the other. He laughs easily and watches everything. His rings are expensive and his smile is professional. He smells of sandalwood and money.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: expensive jade rings on both hands, a gold tooth visible when smiling

desires: To profit from every transaction that crosses his path, whether it is silk, secrets, or stolen documents.
To maintain his neutrality, which is his most valuable asset.
fears_or_limits: He has made enemies on all sides by selling to everyone. His neutrality protects him only as long as no one decides he is more dangerous alive than dead. He is a civilian with no combat skills.

entries.name: Monk Jian Yi
entries.gm_notes: Jian Yi has been cultivating chi for forty years and has reached a level most monks only read about. He can reinforce his body against blades, move faster than the eye follows, and project force at a distance. He has also seen something in meditation that disturbs him: a vision of something deep beneath the world, behind a door, stirring. He does not know what it is. He has begun walking toward Verdania because the vision came with a direction, and the direction is south. He does not know about Shaman Nara's river spirit warning, but he is walking toward her.

payload.summary: A wandering chi monk, old and powerful. A thin, bald man in rough robes who walks barefoot and carries a bamboo staff. He has been cultivating chi for forty years. He does not speak often, but when he does, people listen — sometimes because his words carry spiritual weight, and sometimes because they are unexpectedly funny.
payload.appearance: A thin, wiry man in faded grey robes, barefoot, with a bamboo staff. His head is shaved and tanned by decades of sun. He moves with a fluidity that is subtly wrong for his apparent age — the walk of someone whose body is reinforced by decades of chi cultivation.

visual_identity.age: sixties — moves like someone much younger
visual_identity.distinctive_features: barefoot in all weather, a circular burn-scar on the right palm from a chi cultivation injury

desires: To understand the vision he has been seeing in meditation — something stirring behind a door deep beneath the world.
To reach Verdania, which the vision has been pulling him toward.
fears_or_limits: He does not know what he is walking toward. His chi power is formidable but specific — he can fight, heal, and sense, but he has no political influence and no connections outside the monastic community.

entries.name: Wen Li of the Canals
entries.gm_notes: Wen Li is a river-folk woman who manages the canal system that feeds Jin'an's grain supply. The canals are silting up because the truce diverted maintenance funds to the military. If the canals fail, Jin'an loses its food supply within a season. Wen Li has been writing reports to the warlord's court for two years and has been ignored. She is now considering sabotaging a canal to force the court to pay attention — a desperate act that would cause immediate food shortages but might save the system in the long run. She has not decided yet.

payload.summary: A river-folk canal master who maintains the water system feeding Jin'an's grain supply. A practical, weathered woman who has been fighting for maintenance funding for two years and losing. She knows the canals better than anyone alive, and she knows they are failing.
payload.appearance: A compact river-folk woman in work clothes, her blue-green skin damp, her webbed hands calloused from rope and stone work. She carries a canal surveyor's rod and wears a waterproof jacket. She is usually wet to the elbows.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: webbed fingers and toes, gill-slits along the neck that close on land

desires: To get the canal system repaired before it fails and Jin'an starves.
To prove that infrastructure is as important as armies, which no one in the warlord's court believes.
fears_or_limits: She has no political power and has been ignored for years. Her idea of sabotaging a canal to force attention is becoming more appealing and more desperate. She is a civilian, not a fighter.

entries.name: Warlord Sun Liang
entries.gm_notes: Sun Liang is not a coward — he is a patient man who believes that time is on his side. Chu's economy is growing while Jin and Wei spend on military. He is correct about the economics, but he is wrong about the timeline. Cao Shen's illness means Jin's timeline is shorter than Sun Liang thinks, and Lu Fang's impatience means the truce may break before Chu's economic advantage matures. Sun Liang has also been secretly negotiating with Wei's heir — not for alliance against Jin, but for a future marriage alliance that would merge Chu's wealth with Wei's iron. If it works, the combined state would dominate Sangguo without a war. If Jin finds out, it looks like an alliance against them.

payload.summary: The warlord of Chu, the southern state of Sangguo. A calm, elegant man in his sixties who prefers trade to war and has built Chu's economy into the strongest in Sangguo. He is patient, generous with his allies, and merciless with his enemies' supply lines.
payload.appearance: An elegant man in fine silk robes, a jade pendant at his belt, a fan in his hand. He is slim, composed, and moves with the grace of someone trained in the martial arts who no longer needs to prove it. His beard is white and perfectly groomed.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a jade pendant worn at the belt, ink-calligraphy stains on the right index finger

desires: To make Chu's economic advantage insurmountable before the truce breaks, so that unification happens by merger, not conquest.
To secure a marriage alliance with Wei's heir that would combine their strengths.
fears_or_limits: His strategy requires time, and time may be running out — Jin's military pressure is increasing. The Wei marriage negotiation is delicate and could be interpreted as an act of war by Jin.

entries.name: Apprentice Tari
entries.gm_notes: Tari has a gift that Nara has not seen in thirty years of teaching: she can hear spirits without a formal pact. They speak to her unbidden, sometimes spirits she has no relationship with. This is not entirely a blessing — the spirits do not always say things she wants to hear, and some of them are frightened. Tari has been hearing fragments of the same warning Nara's river spirit gave — 'the deep place' and 'the old door' — but from multiple spirits, not just one. She has not told Nara because she is afraid Nara will say she is too young to understand, and she is also afraid Nara will understand too well and do something dangerous.

payload.summary: A young shaman apprentice in Iara, studying under Shaman Nara. A girl of sixteen who is talented, anxious, and hearing things she does not want to hear. She has a gift for spirit-communication that is emerging faster than her training can keep up with.
payload.appearance: A slight girl in plain river-cloth, her arms not yet marked with pact-patterns — she is too young. Her hair is braided with river-grass, and she carries a pouch of offering-stones. She is usually near the water, listening to it.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: unmarked arms — no pact-patterns yet, a faint blue glow around the fingertips when spirit-listening

desires: To understand what she is hearing from the spirits without losing her apprenticeship or her nerve.
To prove to Nara that she is ready for her first spirit-pact, even though she is afraid.
fears_or_limits: Her gift is emerging faster than her training. She is hearing frightened spirits and does not know how to protect herself from what they are frightened of. She is sixteen and alone with something she does not understand.

entries.name: Kaa the Jaguar-kin
entries.gm_notes: Kaa has found something in the deep jungle: a temple entrance that was not there before. The jungle grew over it centuries ago, and something has cleared the vines away from the door in the last month. The door is stone, carved with symbols he does not recognize, and it is warm to the touch. He did not open it. He came back to Iara to tell Nara, but Nara has been preoccupied with the river spirit's warning and has not listened properly. Kaa is now sitting in a riverside tavern, drinking, and trying to decide whether to go back alone or wait for someone to take him seriously.

payload.summary: A jaguar-kin hunter of Verdania, one of the best in the deep jungle. A tall, powerfully built man with jaguar spots across his skin and yellow eyes. He is quiet, patient, and at home in the jungle in ways that make outsiders nervous.
payload.appearance: A tall, powerful man in minimal jungle gear — a loincloth, a hunter's belt, and a bone-tipped spear. His skin is covered in jaguar-spot patterns, natural to his kin. He moves through the jungle without sound, which is unsettling when you notice it.

visual_identity.skin: tawny brown, rosette spots across the shoulders and back
visual_identity.distinctive_features: jaguar-spot skin markings, elongated canines, a notched left ear from a jungle fight

desires: To understand what he found in the deep jungle — a temple door that was not open before and is warm to the touch.
To get someone to take him seriously enough to go back with a proper team.
fears_or_limits: He is a hunter, not a scholar or a shaman. He does not understand what he found. The jungle is dangerous enough without ancient doors opening on their own. He is drinking, which is not a coping mechanism he can sustain.

entries.name: Dr. Voss Alemann
entries.gm_notes: Voss is from Valdris — a human academic who came to Verdania to study the temple cities. He has been here for three years and has made progress that the local tribes find unsettling: he has been mapping the temple network and has found a pattern that suggests the temples are not random — they form a grid, and the grid converges on a point deep in the jungle that no one has explored. The point is the same direction that Kaa found his warm door, and the same direction Monk Jian Yi is walking. Voss does not know about Kaa or Jian Yi. He wants to mount an expedition, but the tribal council will not authorize it because the deep jungle is sacred ground.

payload.summary: A human academic from Valdris, living in Iara to study the temple cities of the old civilization. A middle-aged man with a scholar's build and an explorer's obsession. He is well-meaning, slightly oblivious to local politics, and deeply curious about things that may be better left alone.
payload.appearance: A thin, sunburnt man in explorer's clothes — canvas trousers, a linen shirt, and a wide hat. He carries a leather satchel full of notebooks and a compass. His Valdris accent is strong and his jungle skills are improving but not great.

visual_identity.skin: pale, sunburnt on the nose and forearms
visual_identity.distinctive_features: round spectacles, a leather satchel always over the shoulder, mosquito bites on both arms

desires: To map the temple network and find the convergence point he has calculated — the place where all the temple sites align.
To prove his theory that the old civilization was not destroyed but deliberately sealed something.
fears_or_limits: The tribal council will not authorize a deep jungle expedition. He is not a fighter and has no survival skills beyond basic camp craft. His obsession with the convergence point is making him careless about local sensitivities.

entries.name: Amara of the Long Boat
entries.gm_notes: Amara is the person who connects Verdania to the outside world. Her boat is one of the few that travels the full river from the Mist Falls to Iara and back. She has noticed that the river's behavior is changing — currents are shifting, fish patterns are altering, and the river spirits she makes small offerings to are restless. She carries mail, news, and goods between the jungle edge and the river capital. She is also Kaa's cousin and has been trying to get him to stop drinking and tell her what he found.

payload.summary: A river-folk trader who runs a long boat between the Mist Falls trading post and Iara. A practical, weathered woman who knows the river the way a wayfinder knows the sea. She carries goods, news, and mail, and she is the closest thing Verdania has to a postal service.
payload.appearance: A stocky river-folk woman in waterproof river-cloth, her blue-green skin wind-dried and sun-darkened. She poles her boat with a strength that surprises people who judge by her height. She wears a necklace of river-stones, one for each year on the water.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: webbed hands, a necklace of seventeen river-stones, a faded tattoo of a river-spirit sigil on the left shoulder

desires: To keep her trade route running as the river changes, and to understand why the river spirits are restless.
To get her cousin Kaa to tell her what he found in the deep jungle before he drinks himself into uselessness.
fears_or_limits: The river is changing and her route may become impassable. She is a trader, not a shaman or a fighter. Her boat is her livelihood and her only asset.

entries.name: Chief Oron of Iara
entries.gm_notes: Oron is a politician, not a shaman. He respects Nara but is tired of her spiritual warnings taking priority over practical problems. The city is flooding, people need housing, and the council spends its time discussing spirit-pacts. He has been quietly building support to relocate Iara upstream, away from the rising river — a massive undertaking that would split the community. He does not believe the river spirit's warning is about something supernatural; he thinks it is about the river flooding, which is a problem engineering can solve, not magic.

payload.summary: The elected chief of Iara, a man in his fifties who governs the river capital. Practical, political, and increasingly frustrated with the shamans' influence over council decisions. He wants to solve the flooding with engineering, not spirit-pacts.
payload.appearance: A stocky, sun-darkened man in fine river-cloth and featherwork — the marks of his office. He carries a chief's staff of carved driftwood. He is usually in the council hall, arguing. He has a loud voice and uses it.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a chief's featherwork collar, a ritual scar on the left cheek marking his election

desires: To relocate Iara upstream before the river takes the lower districts, with or without the council's agreement.
To reduce the shamans' influence over civic decisions, which he believes is keeping the city from acting.
fears_or_limits: The shamans have more influence than he does with the people. Relocating the city splits the community. He may be right about the engineering and wrong about the supernatural — and being wrong about the supernatural in Verdania has consequences.

entries.name: Volva Helga
entries.gm_notes: Helga has seen the same thing in her seidr visions that Shaman Nara's river spirit warned about and Monk Jian Yi has been seeing in meditation: something behind a door, deep beneath the world, stirring. She has also seen something else — a figure walking south through Sangguo, barefoot, which she recognizes as a chi monk of significant power. She does not know who he is, but the vision tells her his path and hers will cross, and that the crossing matters. She has begun traveling toward Verdania, following the vision.

payload.summary: A volva — a wise woman and seer — of Hrafnland. An old woman who reads runes, sees visions, and is respected and slightly feared by everyone in Skaldvik. She lives in a hut outside the town and comes in when the visions demand it. She is currently in Skaldvik because the visions have been demanding it.
payload.appearance: An old woman in layers of wool and fur, a pouch of runestones at her belt. She walks with a staff carved with runes that glow faintly in the dark. Her eyes are milky — her sight is going physical, but her seidr sight is sharper than ever.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: rune-carved staff that glows faintly, clouded eyes, ritual tattoos on both hands

desires: To understand the vision of something stirring behind a door beneath the world, and to find the chi monk she saw walking south.
To reach Verdania, where she believes the door is.
fears_or_limits: Her physical sight is failing. Her visions are becoming more intense and less controlled — they come unbidden now. She is old and the journey to Verdania is long.

entries.name: Tor Longkeel
entries.gm_notes: Tor's wife was on a fishing boat that vanished near the deep fjords two months ago — one of the villages Sigrid has been worried about. The boat was found empty, no signs of violence. Tor has been building a longship in his yard, not for trade but for a voyage into the deep fjords to find her. He has not told Jarl Sigrid because he does not want to be stopped. He has been gathering supplies quietly and has recruited three other men who lost family on the same boat.

payload.summary: A master shipwright in Skaldvik, building longships for the jarl's fleet. A big, quiet man who works with his hands and says what he means. He is currently building a longship in his private yard — not for the jarl, but for himself. He will not say where it is going.
payload.appearance: A big man in a leather apron, sawdust in his beard, his hands huge and calloused from decades of woodwork. He smells of pine tar and wood shavings. He is quiet — not unfriendly, just economical with words.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a woodworker's calluses on both hands, a missing ring finger on the left hand from a saw accident

desires: To find his wife, who vanished on a fishing boat near the deep fjords two months ago.
To build the ship that will take him there, regardless of what the jarl says.
fears_or_limits: He is going into the deep fjords, where Sigrid's scouts have not returned from. He is a shipwright, not a warrior. He is driven by grief, which is not the same as courage.

entries.name: Skald Ravn
entries.gm_notes: Ravn has been composing an epic about the frost giants that is not entirely flattering to the giants — and not entirely accurate, because Ravn has been embellishing for dramatic effect. The giants, who have oral traditions of their own, have heard about the poem and are offended. A giant emissary has come to Skaldvik not to threaten but to complain — formally, in the way that giants complain, which is by sitting outside the settlement and refusing to leave until the offending poem is corrected. Ravn thinks this is hilarious. Sigrid does not.

payload.summary: A skald — a poet and storyteller — of Skaldvik. A thin, dramatic man in his thirties who carries a lyre and a reputation. He knows every saga, can improvise verse on any subject, and has opinions about everything. He is the social glue of the mead hall and the biggest mouth in Hrafnland.
payload.appearance: A thin, animated man in colorful wool — more colorful than is strictly practical in Hrafnland. He carries a lyre everywhere and plays it at every opportunity. His hair is long and he has a performer's sense of when to pause.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a lyre always in hand, ink-stained fingers from composing, a silver ear ring

desires: To compose the greatest saga of his generation — and to survive the political consequences of the sagas he has already composed.
To be the first skald to witness a frost giant up close and live to tell the poem.
fears_or_limits: His poem about the frost giants has offended them, and a giant emissary is sitting outside Skaldvik demanding corrections. He is a poet, not a fighter. His mouth is faster than his judgment.

entries.name: Grimvard the Patient
entries.gm_notes: Grimvard is not a warrior — he is a frost giant elder, a keeper of their oral history. He has come to Skaldvik not to threaten but to correct the record: Ravn's poem has the giants' history wrong, and giants take their history seriously.
