He is sitting outside the town because he is too large for the buildings and because sitting is the giants' way of saying 'I will wait.' He is willing to talk. He is not willing to leave until the poem is corrected. If Sigrid asks the right questions, Grimvard knows things about the deep mountains that her scouts did not survive to report.

payload.summary: A frost giant emissary, sitting outside Skaldvik. Twelve feet tall, grey-skinned, wrapped in furs, patient as stone. He is not here to fight — he is here because a skald's poem got the giants' history wrong, and giants take their sagas seriously. He will wait as long as it takes.
payload.appearance: A towering figure, grey-skinned and broad, wrapped in layers of white fur. He sits cross-legged outside the town walls, his hands on his knees, and does not move. His eyes are pale blue, ancient, and unbothered. He speaks rarely, in a voice like grinding ice.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: ritual scarring on both cheeks, frost crystals in the beard that never melt

desires: To have the skald's poem corrected — the giants' history must be told accurately, or not at all.
To maintain the peace between giants and humans, which he believes serves both peoples.
fears_or_limits: He is one giant sitting outside a human town, and not all humans are as patient as he is. He cannot enter the buildings. His size makes communication awkward and his presence makes people nervous even though he means no harm.

entries.name: Jarl Erik Stone-eye
entries.gm_notes: Erik is Sigrid's rival on the Althing council — a young jarl from the southern fjords who opposes her coalition against the giants. He does not believe the giants are a threat and thinks Sigrid is using them as an excuse to consolidate power. He is not wrong to be suspicious of Sigrid's motives, but he is wrong about the giants. Erik has been quietly gathering support to block Sigrid's coalition at the next Althing, and he has enough support to force a stalemate. He does not know about the abandoned village — if he did, it would change his position.

payload.summary: A young jarl from Hrafnland's southern fjords, in his early thirties. Handsome, opinionated, and suspicious of Sigrid's coalition. He opposes action against the frost giants and believes Sigrid is using the threat to consolidate power. He is a political rival, not an enemy — but rivals can become enemies fast in Hrafnland.
payload.appearance: A young, handsome man in fine fur and iron, a throwing axe at his belt. He has a jarl's bearing and a younger man's certainty. His left eye is pale and unseeing — the stone-eye that gives him his name — and he wears an eyepatch of polished slate.

visual_identity.eyes: right eye blue, left eye pale and unseeing
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a polished slate eyepatch over the left eye, a young jarl's silver arm-ring

desires: To block Sigrid's coalition at the Althing and prevent what he sees as an unnecessary war with the frost giants.
To position himself as the voice of the southern fjords, which feel ignored by the north.
fears_or_limits: He is wrong about the giants' intentions, but his political instincts about Sigrid's consolidation are not entirely wrong. If he blocks action and the giants are a threat, the blood is on his hands. He does not know about the abandoned village.

entries.name: Zuhayr the Patient
entries.gm_notes: Zuhayr is not malicious. He is a djinn of fire and law, and the contract is real — Malik's grandfather agreed to it, and the terms are clear. Zuhayr does not want to collect Malik. He would prefer a renegotiation, because Malik is interesting and a bound servant who resents you is less useful than a willing partner. But the contract has terms, and the terms have a deadline, and Zuhayr cannot extend the deadline unilaterally — djinn law is as binding on djinn as it is on humans. If Malik does not renegotiate before the deadline, Zuhayr must collect. He is, genuinely, on Malik's side, which makes him the most dangerous kind of creditor: one who wants to help but cannot.

payload.summary: A djinn — a fire-spirit of the desert, bound to the Idris family by a contract three generations old. He appears as a figure of blue fire in human form, or as a pillar of flame, or as a man with skin like cracked obsidian. He is patient, polite, and entirely bound by the contract's terms. He has been appearing to Malik to remind him that the deadline is approaching.
payload.role: Djinn, bound by contract to the Idris family
payload.appearance: A figure that shifts between forms — sometimes a man with skin like dark obsidian cracked with lines of blue fire, sometimes a pillar of blue flame wearing clothes, sometimes just heat shimmer in the air. When he chooses a human form, he is tall, composed, and dresses in the style of a desert scholar. His eyes are always fire.

visual_identity.age: ancient — djinn are older than human civilization
visual_identity.skin: dark obsidian with cracks of blue fire (in true form); warm brown (in human form)
visual_identity.hair: black, or flame, depending on form
visual_identity.distinctive_features: skin that sometimes shows cracks of blue fire, a faint smell of ozone and hot sand, heat shimmer around the hands

desires: To resolve the contract with Malik — preferably through renegotiation, because Malik is more useful as a willing partner than as a bound servant. But the deadline is real, and Zuhayr cannot extend it alone.
To maintain the Pact of the Lamp, which preserves the peace between the city-states and which he helped design.
fears_or_limits: He is bound by djinn law as strictly as humans are bound by the contract. He cannot extend the deadline without a renegotiation, and a renegotiation requires Malik to initiate. If the contract is broken by force, the Pact of the Lamp may fracture.

entries.name: Fatima Idris
entries.gm_notes: Fatima discovered Malik's research notes three days ago. She is not bound by the contract — she is the second child — but she has her own reasons for wanting the family's debts exposed: the binding families' power is built on contracts that are quietly crushing them, and Fatima believes the system is unsustainable. She wants to reform the binding families from within, which means breaking the secrecy around the contracts. She is not above using Malik's desperation as a catalyst. She loves her brother, but she also sees him as useful to her larger cause. She has not told Malik she found his notes.

payload.summary: Malik's younger sister, in her late teens. Sharp, political, and frustrated with her family's culture of secrecy. She is not bound by the family's oldest contract — only firstborns are — and she sees that as both a freedom and an injustice. She has opinions about the binding families' system that would scandalize the council.
payload.appearance: A young woman in fine desert robes — deep blue and silver, less flashy than her brother's. She carries a book of contract law under her arm and has ink on her fingers. She is quieter than Malik and pays closer attention. She watches her brother the way a chess player watches a piece.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: ink stains on the right hand from studying contract law, a small silver nose-stud

desires: To reform the binding families' system of djinn contracts, which she believes is secretly destroying them.
To help her brother, but also to use his situation as proof that the system is broken — which means she needs his crisis to become public before she can fix it.
fears_or_limits: She is young and has no political power yet. Exposing the contracts would scandalize the council and could get her disowned. Her brother does not know what she knows, and she has not decided whether to tell him.

entries.name: Layla the Spice Queen
entries.gm_notes: Layla is the richest merchant in Zaffar and sits on the city council. She is not a binder — she has no djinn contracts — but she has built her trade network by being smarter and faster than the binding families, who rely on djinn power instead of business sense. She sees the binding families' debt problem as an opportunity: if they collapse, their trade networks become available. She is not malicious, but she is opportunistic. She has noticed Malik's distress and is watching, waiting to see if the family cracks so she can pick up the pieces. She would also help Malik if he came to her — for a price.

payload.summary: The wealthiest spice merchant in Zaffar, and the only council member who is not a binder. A woman in her sixties who built her trade empire without djinn contracts, through sheer business sense. She is formidable, elegant, and watching the binding families' problems with the patience of a cat at a mouse hole.
payload.appearance: An elegant older woman in rich desert silks — amber and burgundy — with gold jewelry at the wrists and neck. She moves slowly, deliberately, and speaks in a voice that carries across a market without raising. She smells of saffron and authority.

visual_identity.hair: silver, covered by a silk headscarf
visual_identity.distinctive_features: gold bracelets on both wrists, a spice-stain on the left thumb that never quite fades, henna patterns on both hands

desires: To expand her trade network by picking up the pieces if the binding families' system weakens.
To prove that commerce, not djinn power, is the real foundation of Al-Khayzar's prosperity.
fears_or_limits: The binding families still control the Pact of the Lamp, and the djinn enforce it. If she moves too aggressively against them, the djinn may act. She is powerful in trade but has no magical protection.

entries.name: Rashid the Sand-walker
entries.gm_notes: Rashid knows the deep desert better than anyone alive — the routes between oases that do not appear on maps, the places where the sand shifts and the Old Road fragments surface after storms. He has found a working fragment of the Old Road in the deep desert — a short stretch, maybe two hours of walking, that connects the Mirror Oasis to a point near the Verdania border. He has not told anyone because a working Old Road fragment is the most valuable secret in Gaia, and he is deciding who to sell it to. He is also slightly frightened of it, because the fragment hums, and the hum sounds like a voice.

payload.summary: A desert guide in Al-Khayzar who knows the deep desert routes that do not appear on maps. A lean, weathered man who has spent more of his life under the open sky than under a roof. He is quiet, capable, and knows things about the desert that the binding families would pay handsomely to learn.
payload.appearance: A lean, weathered man in desert robes — sun-bleached and sand-worn, wrapped against the heat. His face is deeply lined and his eyes are narrowed against a sun that is no longer there. He carries a waterskin and a staff and moves through sand as if it were pavement.

visual_identity.hair: black, greying, wrapped in a desert headwrap
visual_identity.distinctive_features: sun-wrinkles deep around the eyes, a sand-scar on the left cheek from a dust storm, a tattoo of a compass rose on the right forearm

desires: To sell his knowledge of the working Old Road fragment to the right person for the right price.
To understand why the fragment hums like a voice, which is not how Old Roads are supposed to behave.
fears_or_limits: A working Old Road fragment is the most valuable secret in Gaia, and everyone he tells becomes a threat or a competitor. The hum frightens him — Old Roads are silent, and this one is not.

entries.name: Judge Tariq al-Mir
entries.gm_notes: Tariq is the Pact of the Lamp's enforcer — not through violence but through law. He is the judge who interprets contract disputes between binding families and djinn. He is honest, incorruptible, and absolutely bound by precedent. If Malik comes to him for a legal remedy, Tariq will help — but only within the law, and the law may not have a remedy for a contract this old. Tariq has noticed that the oldest contracts are becoming unstable — the djinn are restive, the terms are fraying, and the precedent he relies on was written for a world that no longer exists. He is worried, and a worried judge in Al-Khayzar is a dangerous thing.

payload.summary: A judge of Al-Khayzar, the foremost authority on contract law and the Pact of the Lamp. A tall, grave man in judge's robes — dark blue and gold — who speaks in measured sentences and means every word. He is honest, which in Zaffar makes him unusual, and he is worried, which in Zaffar makes him dangerous.
payload.role: Judge, expert in contract law and the Pact
payload.appearance: A tall, grave man in formal judge's robes, a law scroll case at his belt. He moves deliberately, speaks precisely, and has the stillness of someone who has spent decades listening to liars. His beard is white and trimmed. He carries the law the way soldiers carry swords.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a judge's signet ring on the right index finger, ink stains on the left hand, a small scar on the forehead from a courtroom incident years ago

desires: To maintain the Pact of the Lamp and the legal order it provides, which is the only thing keeping Al-Khayzar's city-states from war.
To find a legal remedy for the oldest djinn contracts before they begin to break — because when contracts break in Al-Khayzar, djinn collect, and collection is not always clean.
fears_or_limits: The law may not have a remedy for Malik's contract — it was written three generations ago under different precedents. He is honest, which means he will not bend the law to help someone he sympathizes with. His integrity is his strength and his limitation.

entries.name: Chief Lani of Lani Atoll
entries.gm_notes: Lani is Kai's mother — a fact she has deliberately kept out of her governance to avoid accusations of nepotism, and which Kai has respected by never invoking it publicly. She is the one who must decide what happens to the forty families displaced by the latest island submergence, and she has nowhere to put them. She has been secretly negotiating with Verdania's Chief Oron to accept island refugees, which would be politically explosive if the other islands found out — the Archipelago's identity is built on self-sufficiency.

payload.summary: The chief of Lani Atoll, the central gathering island of the Tide Archipelago. A woman in her fifties who has led her island through twenty years of gradual crisis. She is warm, decisive, and carrying more than she shows. The meeting house on her island is still open to all, but the shore is closer to the door than it was last year.
payload.appearance: A sturdy, sun-darkened woman in fine island cloth and a chief's whale-bone necklace. She moves with the authority of someone who has been making hard decisions for decades. Her arms are tattooed with the route-maps of her youth — she was a wayfinder before she was a chief.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: a chief's whale-bone necklace, wayfinder tattoos on both arms (faded), a small scar on the left calf from a shark encounter

desires: To find a home for the displaced islanders before the next storm displaces more.
To keep the Archipelago's community intact through the crisis — self-sufficiency is their identity, and asking for outside help would change who they are.
fears_or_limits: She is secretly negotiating with Verdania for refugee placement, which would be politically explosive. She is Kai's mother and cannot favor him publicly. The water is still rising and her options are shrinking.

entries.name: Elder Wayfinder Pua
entries.gm_notes: Pua is the keeper of the oldest songs — the deep-water songs that can call whales, calm storms, and, according to legends she does not share publicly, speak to the sea itself. She has not sung the deepest song in forty years because the last time she did, the sea answered, and the answer frightened her. The sea is not a spirit in the way river spirits are — it is vast, old, and does not think in the way people think. It responded to the song with something that was not words but was not silence, and Pua has been careful not to sing it again. She is now considering whether the rising seas require her to sing it, despite the risk.

payload.summary: An elder wayfinder, the oldest in the Archipelago. A woman in her seventies who has sailed every route and sung every song. She taught Kai and most of the active wayfinders. She is small, quiet, and carries more knowledge than anyone realizes — including songs she has never taught because she is afraid of what they do.
payload.appearance: A small, weathered woman in simple island cloth, her arms covered in faded tattoos so old they have blurred to blue shadows. She carries a wayfinder's staff that is older than she is, dark with salt and handling. She moves slowly but her eyes are sharp.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: faded tattoo patterns covering both arms — the oldest routes, barely visible, a wayfinder's staff dark with age

desires: To decide whether to sing the deepest song — the one that speaks to the sea itself — to ask why the water is rising.
To pass on the old songs before she dies, including the ones she has never taught, which means finding someone she trusts with dangerous knowledge.
fears_or_limits: The last time she sang the deepest song, the sea answered in a way that frightened her. She is old and may not survive the strain of singing it again. The songs she has never taught could be misused — they are powerful, and power in the wrong hands is worse than no power.

entries.name: Mana the Tattoo-carver
entries.gm_notes: Mana's tattoo work is more than art — each route-map she carves into a wayfinder's skin creates a real connection between the wayfinder and the routes. When a route is lost to rising seas, the wayfinder who carries it feels the loss as a physical ache in the tattoo. Mana has been feeling aches in her own arms all year — she carries twenty routes, and three have gone silent. She believes the route-maps are not just records but anchors — that the tattoos help hold the routes in existence. If the tattoos fade or the wayfinder dies, the route weakens. She has not told the guild because the implication is that wayfinders are not just navigating the sea — they are holding it together, and that is a burden the guild is not ready to hear.

payload.summary: The tattoo artist of Lani Atoll, a woman in her forties who carves the route-maps into wayfinders' skin. Her work is art, craft, and something more — the tattoos are not just records, they are connections. She is quiet, skilled, and carrying a theory about the rising seas that no one has asked her for.
payload.appearance: A stocky woman in work clothes, her arms covered in the tattoo patterns she has carved on others — a tradition that artists carry the routes they inscribe. She holds a bone tattooing needle and ink made from volcanic soot. Her hands are steady and her eyes are kind.

visual_identity.distinctive_features: tattoo patterns covering both arms — twenty routes, three faded where islands have submerged, a bone tattooing needle always in hand or behind the ear

desires: To understand why the tattoos that mark submerged routes are aching — and whether the wayfinders are holding the sea-routes in existence by carrying them.
To preserve the route-maps before more are lost, which means carving them on more people, which means teaching more wayfinders.
fears_or_limits: Her theory — that wayfinder tattoos are anchors for the routes themselves — implies that the rising seas are connected to the loss of wayfinders and routes, not just the other way around. This is a dangerous idea. She is an artist, not a scholar, and she does not know how to prove it.

entries.name: Fin the Whale-speaker
entries.gm_notes: Fin has been hearing something from the whales that frightens him: the great whales are leaving. Not migrating — leaving. They are swimming south, past the Archipelago, past Verdania, toward the open southern ocean, and they are not coming back. The whales have been the Archipelago's allies for centuries — they guide wayfinders, warn of storms, and carry messages. Without them, voyaging becomes vastly more dangerous. Fin has tried to ask why they are leaving. The whales answer in images, not words, and the images they have been sending are: deep water, a door, and something behind it that is waking up. The same images Nara's river spirit sent, the same vision Jian Yi and Helga have seen.

payload.summary: A young man of the Tide Archipelago who can speak to whales — a rare gift that runs in certain families. He is in his early twenties, quiet, and uncomfortable with the attention his gift brings. He is usually found at the water's edge, listening to things that are too far away for anyone else to hear.
payload.appearance: A lean young man in simple island cloth, barefoot, sitting at the water's edge. He has the distant look of someone who is always half-listening to something else. His skin is dark and his hair is salt-bleached. He carries a conch shell horn for calling whales.

visual_identity.hair: bleached blonde from salt and sun, shaggy
visual_identity.distinctive_features: a conch shell horn worn on a cord around the neck, webbed toes (a minor birth trait common in whale-speaker families), a far-listening expression

desires: To understand why the whales are leaving the Archipelago — they have been allies for centuries and their departure endangers everyone.
To translate what the whales are showing him — images of deep water, a door, and something waking — into something people can act on.
fears_or_limits: The whales are leaving and he cannot stop them. The images they send are not words — he has to interpret them, and he is not certain he is interpreting correctly. He is young and his gift isolates him — most people think whale-speaking is a myth.

_help: Bonds between people. Keep the shared and private halves separate:
`public_status` is what anyone can observe; `bond` is your assessment and
stays GM-side.
`disposition` is a number from -100 to 100. It is stored today and does
not drift on its own yet (Phase 2, W2.3).

entries.name: Sir Aldrich and the Dragon Order

payload.public_status: A respected senior knight, loyal to the order, though quiet at council meetings.
payload.bond: Aldrich is losing faith in the order's ability to resolve its own crisis. He stays because leaving would confirm the traditionalists' fears, but he is privately sympathetic to the reformers. His silence at council meetings is not loyalty — it is indecision.

entries.name: Cao Shen and General Lu Fang

payload.public_status: Cao Shen trusts Lu Fang with military command. Lu Fang is publicly loyal and has never failed an order.
payload.bond: Cao Shen suspects Lu Fang's loyalty is to the idea of a unified Sangguo, not specifically to Cao Shen. If Cao Shen dies before reunification, Lu Fang may pursue it himself — in his own way, which may be less careful.

payload.public_status: The king's two eldest children, publicly civil, privately competing for the succession. The court watches them and bets quietly.
payload.bond: Elara underestimates Roderick's cunning — she thinks he is a blunt soldier, but he has been feeding her false intelligence through a double agent. Roderick does not know about Elara's dragonbone research, which is the one card she has that he cannot counter. They are siblings and they are enemies, and neither of them has decided which matters more.

payload.public_status: Two jarls who disagree about the frost giant threat. Sigrid wants action; Erik wants restraint. The Althing watches them and waits.
payload.bond: Sigrid thinks Erik is naive about the giants. Erik thinks Sigrid is using the giants to consolidate power. Both are partly right, which makes the rivalry productive and dangerous. If the abandoned village goes public, Erik's position collapses and Sigrid wins — which is why Sigrid has been sitting on the information.

entries.name: Malik Idris and Zuhayr the Patient

payload.public_status: Malik is the heir to the Idris family's oldest djinn contract. Zuhayr is the djinn bound by it. The contract's terms are family knowledge but not public.
payload.bond: Zuhayr genuinely wants to help Malik renegotiate — a willing partner is more useful than a bound servant. But the contract's deadline is binding on both of them, and neither can extend it alone. Zuhayr is the most dangerous kind of ally: one who is on Malik's side but constrained by law from giving him more time. Their relationship is warm in a way that makes the debt more painful, not less.

payload.public_status: A young wayfinder and the chief of Lani Atoll. They maintain professional distance in public, as a chief should not favor one wayfinder over others.
payload.bond: They are mother and son, and both know it, and neither says it in public. Kai respects his mother's governance and does not want to compromise it. Lani is proud of her son and frightened for him — he is sailing toward something neither of them understands. Their private relationship is warm; their public one is careful.

payload.public_status: Nara is training Tari in the shamanic traditions. Tari is young and talented. A normal master-apprentice relationship.
payload.bond: Nara knows Tari is gifted but does not realize how much Tari is hearing that Nara is not. Tari is afraid of being dismissed as too young, and afraid of being taken seriously. They trust each other but are both keeping secrets — Nara about the river spirit's warning, Tari about the multiple spirits speaking to her. The secrets are about the same thing, and neither knows the other already knows.

payload.public_status: No public relationship. A daimyo and a wild kitsune would not be seen together.
payload.bond: Takeda thinks he is using Tamamo to create yokai incidents that prove the shrine network's weakness. Tamamo is using Takeda to weaken the wards she hates. Neither trusts the other. Both believe they are the one in control. They are both wrong.

entries.name: Garrick the Wolf and Maggie Pippin

payload.association: bandit and innkeeper, uneasy mutual tolerance
payload.public_status: Maggie's inn is on the Greywood road, which Garrick controls. He does not rob her. She does not report him. A practical arrangement.
payload.bond: Maggie feeds Garrick information about travelers in exchange for him keeping the road safe from other bandits. She does not approve of his methods but recognizes that his presence is better than the alternative. Garrick is protective of the inn in a way he would not admit — Maggie reminds him of his mother, who ran a similar inn before the war.

entries.name: Skald Ravn and Grimvard the Patient

payload.public_status: A frost giant is sitting outside Skaldvik because the skald's poem got the giants' history wrong. Ravn thinks it is funny. Everyone else is nervous.
payload.bond: Grimvard respects Ravn's skill as a poet — the poem is beautiful, it is just inaccurate. Ravn is beginning to realize that the giant is not threatening but correcting, and that the corrections contain information about the deep mountains that no human scout has brought back. They are on the verge of a conversation that could change Hrafnland's understanding of the frost giants entirely.

_help: The engine of the campaign. A thread is something unresolved that will
get worse if ignored.
`next_possible_moves` is the most valuable field in this file. Write the
two or three things that could happen NEXT if the player does nothing.
It is what stops a scene ending on a still frame, and you should revise
it as the campaign moves.
`pressure` here IS live. `stakes` is what is lost if it resolves badly.

payload.summary: A soul new to Gaia has arrived in the Heavenly Realm. The Guide is waiting to help them choose a nation to begin in. The choice is real and permanent — once they walk down into one of the seven nations, they cannot come back to choose again.
payload.stakes: The player's starting nation determines which conflicts they land in the middle of, which people they meet first, and what kind of life they begin. A wrong choice is not death — it is a different story.
next_possible_moves: The Guide describes each of the seven nations in a sentence or two and asks where the player wants to begin.
If the player hesitates, the Guide offers to describe one in more detail — but only one.
If the player asks too many questions, the Guide gently reminds them that the choice is meant to be partly blind.

payload.summary: In Valdris, no new dragon bond has been made in twenty years. The dragon-bonded knights are fracturing between reformers and traditionalists. The king is aging and the succession is unspoken. Sir Aldrich's own dragon, Verath, has gone silent — a secret he keeps because admitting it would confirm the order's worst fears.
payload.stakes: If the order fractures completely, Valdris loses its most powerful defenders. If the succession crisis hits while the order is broken, the kingdom could face civil war. Aldrich's secret, if exposed, accelerates both.
next_possible_moves: The reformist faction calls a formal vote to dissolve the traditional oath requirements, which the traditionalists have promised to refuse — publicly and loudly.
Sir Aldrich's dragon Verath descends from the mountain roosts for the first time in three years and lands in the Dragonrest courtyard, silent, refusing to speak to anyone — including Aldrich.
The king's eldest son visits Dragonrest to 'inspect the order,' a move the traditionalists see as a threat and the reformers see as an opportunity.

payload.summary: The three-year truce between Jin, Chu, and Wei is nearing its end. One border skirmish has already happened between Jin and Wei forces at the Long Pass. The younger officers at the Great Academy in Jin'an speak openly about ending the truce. Warlord Cao Shen is dying faster than anyone knows and wants reunification before he goes.
payload.stakes: If the truce breaks, the largest war in a generation begins. The last war killed tens of thousands. Sangguo's trade routes feed half of Gaia — a war disrupts everything, everywhere.
next_possible_moves: A second skirmish at the Long Pass — this time with casualties on both sides, each blaming the other.
Cao Shen's court physician is found dead in the palace, an apparent suicide that the warlord's spymaster does not believe was suicide.
Chu's warlord Sun Liang receives a secret envoy from Wei proposing an alliance against Jin — and the envoy is intercepted by Jin scouts.

payload.summary: In the Tide Archipelago, sea levels are rising. Islands are losing their shores. The voyagers are being pushed inward toward crowded volcanic islands. Wayfinder Kai has lost three routes this year and the sea spirits have gone silent when asked about the cause. In Verdania, Shaman Nara's river spirit has sent a warning it does not fully understand — and the two problems may be connected.
payload.stakes: If the rising continues, the Tide Archipelago loses its civilization within a generation. If the cause is something that can be stopped, every month of delay costs islands. If it cannot be stopped, the voyagers become refugees in nations that do not want them.
next_possible_moves: Two more outer islets submerge during a storm, displacing forty families who arrive at Lani Atoll with nothing.
Kai attempts a solo voyage to the deepest water in the Archipelago to sing to the sea spirits directly — and they answer, but not in words he recognizes.
Shaman Nara's river spirit delivers a fragment of a warning that mentions 'the deep place' and 'the old door,' phrases it has never used before.

payload.summary: In Al-Khayzar, Malik Idris is the firstborn of his generation — and his family's oldest djinn contract demands the firstborn of each generation as payment. The djinn Zuhayr has begun appearing to Malik, patient and polite, reminding him that the contract is almost due. Malik has searched secretly for a way out and found nothing.
payload.stakes: If Malik cannot break or renegotiate the contract, he is taken by the djinn — not killed, but bound to Zuhayr's service for the rest of his natural life. If he breaks the contract wrongly, the Pact of the Lamp may fracture, and the peace between Al-Khayzar's city-states dies with it.
next_possible_moves: Zuhayr appears to Malik in the Star Bazaar, visible to other binders for the first time, making the debt publicly known — which Malik's family will treat as a deliberate humiliation.
Malik's younger sister discovers his research notes and confronts him — she is not bound by the contract, but she has her own reasons for wanting the family's debts exposed.
A stranger arrives in Zaffar claiming to know a method of contract renegotiation that does not violate the Pact — and asking a price that may be worse than the djinn's.

payload.summary: In Tsukuyomi, the shrine network that keeps wild yokai at a distance from settled areas is weakening. Rural shrines are being neglected as the central authority funnels resources to the capital. Miko Sora maintains her shrine alone, but the ward she tends is one of a chain, and links upstream of her are failing. If enough links break, the yokai pressure on the Cedar Road becomes dangerous.
payload.stakes: If the ward chain breaks along the Cedar Road, the pilgrimage route becomes unsafe and the mountain villages lose their protection. Wild yokai are not monsters — they are unpredictable, and people die when the boundary is weak.
next_possible_moves: Sora notices the upstream shrine's ward has gone dark — the keeper there has left, and no replacement was sent.
A farmer from the next valley arrives in Haru's Shrine Town reporting yokai sightings on the Cedar Road — something that has not happened in a generation.
A messenger from the Great Shrine in Tsuki-no-Miyako arrives with an order: Sora is to report to the capital for reassignment. Her shrine will be 'temporarily' unstaffed.

payload.summary: In Hrafnland, Jarl Sigrid believes the frost giants of the deep mountains are preparing to expand southward. She has been quietly building a coalition of jarls who want to push the giants back. The Althing will not authorize action without proof, and proof requires scouting territory no scout has returned from. Her coalition is not as unified as she presents it.
payload.stakes: If Sigrid acts without Althing approval, she splits Hrafnland and may trigger a jarls' war. If she does nothing and the giants are expanding, the northern fjords are overrun. If she is wrong about the giants' intentions, she has spent political capital on a phantom threat.
next_possible_moves: A trader from a northern fjord arrives in Skaldvik with a story: a fishing village was found abandoned, the boats still at the dock, no sign of violence — and no sign of the people.
One of Sigrid's coalition jarls privately withdraws his support, telling her the Althing will see her coalition as a power grab, not a defense.
A scout Sigrid sent into the deep mountains returns — the first to return — and will not speak about what he saw. He has gone white-haired and will not leave the mead hall.

payload.summary: Kuro the Smoke, a cat-folk thief in Tsuki-no-Miyako, stole a document from a daimyo's estate that contains evidence of Takeda's coalition plans. He does not understand what he has, but Takeda's agents are hunting him. The document's trail leads through the underworld of Tsukuyomi and potentially to Sangguo's information broker Zhou Ba, who would sell it to the highest bidder.
payload.stakes: If Takeda's agents recover the document, Kuro is dead and the coalition remains secret. If Zhou Ba sells it to Cao Shen, Sangguo gains leverage over Tsukuyomi's internal politics. If it goes public, the shogunate cracks down on the provincial clans and the coalition goes underground or open revolt.
next_possible_moves: Takeda's agents trace Kuro to the merchant district and close the gates, starting a block-by-block search.
Kuro contacts a middleman to reach Zhou Ba in Sangguo, not knowing that the middleman is also working for Takeda.
Shogun Ashikara's spymaster independently learns that a document was stolen from a daimyo's estate and begins his own investigation — the shogun wants to know what Takeda is hiding.

payload.summary: King Aldran is dying and has not named an heir. Princess Elara backs the reformist faction and secret dragonbone research. Prince Roderick commands the military and is secretly courting the bandit lord Garrick as a deniable asset. The youngest, Tomas, is unaligned. The court is a cold war of positioning, and the king is running out of time.
payload.stakes: If the king dies without naming an heir, civil war. If Roderick wins, the old order hardens and the reformists are purged. If Elara wins, the dragon order is reformed and the old nobility loses power. If Tomas wins — no one knows, including Tomas.
next_possible_moves: The king's physician quietly informs the court that the king's condition is worsening — the information leaks within a day.
Roderick makes Garrick a formal offer: pardon and a commission in exchange for blocking the Greywood road against Elara's merchant allies.
Elara's reformist researchers achieve a partial resonance from a dragonbone artifact — the first proof that an artificial bond might be possible — and someone in her team talks.

payload.summary: Garrick the Wolf controls a stretch of the Greywood road in Valdris. He is being courted by Prince Roderick as a deniable asset. Maggie Pippin at the Copper Kettle has noticed increased armed traffic. The crown's patrols are getting more aggressive. Garrick's men are hungry and loyal, but loyalty has a shelf life.
payload.stakes: If Garrick accepts Roderick's offer, Roderick gains a deniable military asset on the main trade road. If the crown catches Garrick first, his men scatter and the road becomes truly lawless. If Garrick finds another path — a pardon from the king directly, or a war that needs soldiers — the equation changes entirely.
next_possible_moves: A crown patrol ambushes one of Garrick's foraging parties, killing two men — the first blood on the road this season, and it demands a response.
Roderick sends a sealed letter through Maggie's inn offering terms: full pardon, a captain's commission, and control of the road in exchange for blocking Elara's merchant traffic.
Garrick's second-in-command, a woman named Brita, challenges his leadership at a campfire meeting — she wants to accept Roderick's offer and argues that waiting is dying.

payload.summary: Wen Li, the river-folk canal master in Jin'an, has been warning that the canal system feeding the city's grain supply is failing. Two years of ignored reports and diverted maintenance funds have brought the system to the edge. Wen Li is considering sabotage to force the court's attention.
payload.stakes: If the canals fail, Jin'an loses its grain supply within a season. Two hundred thousand people face famine. If Wen Li sabotages a canal to prove her point, the shortage is immediate but the political will to repair is forced. Either way, people suffer.
next_possible_moves: A canal gate fails during a moderate rain, flooding a market district — a preview of what a full failure looks like, and a warning Wen Li did not engineer.
Wen Li's written report is finally read by Strategist Mei Lin, who realizes the canal crisis connects to the truce: military spending has been eating infrastructure budgets for three years.
General Lu Fang orders the canal workers conscripted into military labor, arguing that fortifying the Long Pass is more urgent than canal maintenance. Wen Li is not consulted.

payload.summary: Kaa the Jaguar-kin found a temple door in the deep jungle of Verdania that was not open before and is warm to the touch. Dr. Voss has calculated a convergence point in the same area. Shaman Nara's river spirit has warned of 'the deep place' and 'the old door.' Monk Jian Yi is walking south toward the same location. Volva Helga has seen it in visions. Multiple independent sources are converging on the same point.
payload.stakes: If the door is opening on its own, something is changing beneath the world. If multiple people are being drawn to it independently, the door may be calling them — or whatever is behind the door is. What is behind it is unknown, but everything touching it — river spirits, sea spirits, whales, chi monks, volva, and shamans — is frightened.
next_possible_moves: Kaa goes back to the door alone, drunk and armed, and this time it is open — warm air pouring out of it, carrying a smell like deep water and old stone.

Jian Yi arrives at the Mist Falls trading post on the edge of Verdania, the first leg of his journey complete, and asks a trader about the temple cities — the trader is Amara, Kaa's cousin, who connects him to Iara.
Shaman Nara's river spirit delivers a new warning: the door is not opening because something is pushing from outside. Something is pushing from inside.

payload.summary: Fatima Idris has discovered her brother Malik's research into breaking the family's djinn contract. She wants to use his crisis to expose the binding families' unsustainable contract system and force reform. She has not told Malik what she knows. Judge Tariq is independently worried about the oldest contracts destabilizing. Layla the Spice Queen is watching, ready to pick up the pieces.
payload.stakes: If Fatima exposes the contracts publicly, the binding families lose face and the council fractures — reform or chaos. If Malik breaks his contract badly, the Pact of the Lamp may fail and the city-states' peace dies. If Judge Tariq finds a legal remedy, there is a path through the law — but the law may not have one.
next_possible_moves: Fatima anonymously leaks a summary of the Idris family's oldest contract to a merchant in the Star Bazaar — not the full text, but enough to start rumors.
Judge Tariq summons Malik to his court, not as a defendant but as a consultant — he wants to understand the Idris contract's structure because it is the oldest and may be the first to break.
Zuhayr appears to Malik in public, at the Star Bazaar, visible to other binders — making the debt common knowledge and forcing the family to acknowledge it.

payload.summary: Rashid the Sand-walker has found a working fragment of the Old Road in the deep desert of Al-Khayzar — a two-hour stretch connecting the Mirror Oasis to a point near the Verdania border. The fragment hums like a voice, which is not how Old Roads behave. He is deciding who to tell, and the hum is getting louder.
payload.stakes: A working Old Road fragment is the most valuable secret in Gaia — it could connect Al-Khayzar to Verdania in hours instead of months. If the hum is a voice, the Road may be doing something Old Roads are not supposed to do. If the wrong person learns about it, the secret becomes a weapon.
next_possible_moves: Rashid returns to the fragment to find that the hum has changed — it is now a rhythm, almost a heartbeat, and the air above the Road is shimmering.
A binding family agent notices Rashid's absences and follows him to the Mirror Oasis, not to the fragment itself but close enough to suspect something.
The fragment extends — the Road is growing, clearing itself, pushing back the sand, and the hum is now audible from the oasis.

payload.summary: Fin the Whale-speaker has learned that the great whales are leaving the Tide Archipelago — not migrating, but departing permanently. They are swimming south, past Verdania, toward the open ocean. The images they send him — deep water, a door, something waking — match the warnings from Shaman Nara, Monk Jian Yi, and Volva Helga. Without the whales, voyaging in the Archipelago becomes vastly more dangerous.
payload.stakes: If the whales leave, the Archipelago loses its oldest allies and voyaging becomes far more dangerous. The displaced islanders cannot be relocated if the sea routes are unsafe. Whatever is driving the whales south is connected to the same force that is opening doors and frightening spirits across the world.
next_possible_moves: The last family of whales in the northern Archipelago sends a final image to Fin — a clear picture of the door, from the other side, showing something behind it that is large and moving — then the whales turn south and are gone.
Kai's attempt to sing to the sea spirits at the deepest water goes wrong: the spirits answer, but not in words he recognizes, and the current around his boat changes direction against the wind.
Elder Wayfinder Pua announces to the guild that she will sing the deepest song — the one she has not sung in forty years — and the guild argues about whether it is safe.

payload.summary: Daimyo Takeda Renji is building a coalition of rural clans who feel the shogunate has abandoned them. He has a secret alliance with the wild kitsune Tamamo, who is willing to create yokai incidents to prove the shrine network's weakness. His plans were stolen by the thief Kuro, and the document is now in play. The shogun is dying and the succession is undecided.
payload.stakes: If Takeda's coalition succeeds in forcing the shogunate's hand, the provinces gain power and the shrine network is repaired — but Takeda is positioned as kingmaker. If the coalition is exposed prematurely, it becomes a rebellion. If Tamamo engineers a yokai incident that kills people, Takeda's legitimate grievance becomes a bloody opportunism.
next_possible_moves: Tamamo engineers a yokai breach on the Cedar Road — nothing fatal, but enough to frighten pilgrims and prove the wards are weak. Takeda uses the incident at the next clan council to argue that the shogunate has failed.
The shogun's spymaster traces the stolen document to Takeda's estate and begins investigating the daimyo's coalition — quietly, because accusing a daimyo without proof is a political act.

The shogun's elder son, Ashikara Kenji, confronts Takeda at court — not about the coalition, which he does not know about, but about the yokai incident, which he blames on Takeda's territory being poorly defended. The irony is not lost on Takeda.

payload.summary: Mana the Tattoo-carver believes that wayfinder tattoos are not just records — they are anchors. When a route is submerged and the tattoo fades, the wayfinder feels it as physical pain. She suspects the tattoos are helping hold the sea-routes in existence, and that losing wayfinders and routes may be connected to the rising seas, not just a consequence of them.
payload.stakes: If Mana is right, the wayfinders are not just navigating the sea — they are holding it together, and the loss of routes is accelerating the rising waters. This would mean the Archipelago's crisis is partly self-reinforcing: lose an island, lose a route, lose a wayfinder, lose more sea. If she is wrong, it is a theory that wastes precious time.
next_possible_moves: Mana presents her theory to Elder Wayfinder Pua, who takes it seriously — because Pua has suspected something similar for forty years and has never said so.
A wayfinder carrying a faded route-tattoo collapses during a voyage, screaming about pain in the tattoo — the first time the effect has been visible to witnesses, not just felt by the carrier.
Mana begins carving a new set of route-tattoos on Kai, including a route that was lost last month — to test whether carrying a lost route on a living wayfinder can restore it.

_help: Prose. Religions, histories, laws, languages, how the world got here.
Do not reach for a record here unless something must point at it, be
counted, appear in a panel, or be hidden from the player. Until then a
paragraph in your world/*.md files is better — see MIGRATING.md.
`context_tier` controls whether the narrator may reason about it:
pinned (always) / partial (one line) / searchable / hidden.

payload.summary: Occasionally a person arrives in Gaia carrying memories of another life — another world entirely. These souls are rare, perhaps one in a generation. They arrive in the Heavenly Realm, where a guide helps them choose a nation to begin in. They are called god-touched, and the name is both a compliment and a warning. They often grow into remarkable people, and just as often into troubled ones.

A vanished network of spirit-paths that once connected every nation in Gaia. Walking a working stretch can take you across the world in an afternoon. Most are broken. Some are lost. A few are deliberately kept shut by the people who live near them. Finding a working entrance is valuable. Using one is noticeable — the Roads leave a trace that certain people can follow.

A generation of relative peace across Gaia, following the last great war between Sangguo's states. The peace is uneven — some nations prosper, others simmer. The treaty that ended the war is fraying, and not everyone remembers why it was signed. The current generation is the first to grow up without war, and some of them do not understand what they would be losing.

_help: Objects worth naming. `appearance` feeds the image pipeline; keep story
and provenance in `description`, which the pipeline never reads.

payload.appearance: Small metal discs, about the width of a thumbnail, stamped with the mark of the minting nation. Each is slightly different — Tsukuyomi's carry a crescent moon, Valdris's a crown, Sangguo's a jade-inset square. They are traded by weight, not by origin.
payload.description: The closest thing Gaia has to a universal currency. Accepted across all seven nations by weight. Each nation mints its own, but the metal content is standardized by an old trade agreement that most nations still honor.

payload.appearance: A strip of paper, about the length of a hand, with brush-written characters in black ink. Some carry a red stamp at the bottom. They are usually folded and carried in pockets or pinned to doorframes.
payload.description: The basic tool of shrine magic in Tsukuyomi. An ofuda carries a ward, a blessing, or a command. It must be written correctly and activated by a shrine keeper's ritual. A poorly made ofuda is just paper.

payload.appearance: A carved wooden staff, about shoulder-height, marked with notches and painted symbols that represent star paths, current patterns, and island positions. The wood is dark from salt and handling. Some staves have shells or bone inlays.
payload.description: The primary tool of a wayfinder in the Tide Archipelago. The staff is both a record of routes memorized and an instrument for reading the sea. A wayfinder who loses their staff loses years of encoded knowledge.

_help: The opening. One campaign is created from this; you can make more later
in the app.
`player_name` and `character_class` are the player's, and the engine
builds their character record. `current_location` must be one of the
location ids above.
campaign.title: The Arrival
campaign.current_quest: Choose which of the seven nations to begin your new life in.
campaign.opening_scene: You wake in a garden you have never seen. The air is warm and still, and the light comes from no direction you can find. Floating islands drift in soft mist around you, and flowers bloom in colors that do not belong to the same season. Ahead, through a grove of trees that are not quite real, stands an open pavilion. A figure is waiting there, seated on the stone bench, watching you with patient dark eyes. Below the pavilion, far below, through layers of cloud, you can see a world spread out — green and gold and blue and white. Seven nations. The figure speaks: 'You have arrived. That is well. I have been waiting. Come, and choose where you will begin.'
